title: fix(tui): clarify kickstart privacy step copy and git-remote example
body: ## Problem The `peasant kickstart` privacy step had three issues (`internal/tui/kickstart`): 1. The intro was four lines — too much for a first-run user. 2. The `PII` category label was unexplained. 3. **Bug: the git-remote example rendered as ``.** The project sample was a quoted `"github.com/example-org/example-repo"`, which matches the `go_import_path` rule (replacement ``). The git-remote rules (`git_remote_https` / `git_remote_ssh`) are `Maximum`-only, so they never fire in the Standard preview. Meanwhile the intro claimed "standard keeps git remote urls" while showing a redacted `github.com` path — a direct contradiction. ## Root cause of `` and the chosen fix At `Standard`, the only project-category rules that fire on a `github.com` string are `go_import_path` / `go_module_path` — not the git-remote rules, which are `Minimum​Level: Maximum` in the `github.com/peasant-labs/redact` module. A **real** git-remote URL (`https://github.com/...`) therefore cannot change at Standard, and the privacy example's fail-closed guard requires each category sample to actually change (`after != before`). So a git-remote sample cannot be shown as a Standard before/after without a redact-module change, which is out of scope for this issue. I fixed it by **correcting the guidance** (the issue's second, explicitly-blessed option) rather than swapping the sample: - The project sample stays the Go import path, which is a truthful project-identity redaction that genuinely fires at Standard (``). - The guidance now says **"standard hides project identity but keeps git remotes until maximum,"** which matches the rendered example and gives a user with a git remote a truthful mental model (their remotes are kept at Standard; removed at Maximum). ## Changes - **Simplified intro** (`registry.go`): one ASD-STE100 sentence — "preview how standard redaction changes your text before you publish." — plus two short hints; the detail lives in the rendered before/after example. - **PII spelled out** on first use: a hint reads "personally identifiable information (PII), such as an email address." The canonical redact rendering (`redact.CategoryPII.String()` → `"PII"`) for the example label is unchanged; only the guidance prose gained the expansion. (Prose is lowercase to match the step's house style; the acronym stays uppercase to match the adjacent canonical `PII` label.) - **Example/intro now agree** — no more "keeps git remote urls" beside a redacted github path. ## Tests - New fixture-backed guide-copy contract test `TestPrivacyGuideCopyContract` (`privacy_copy_test.go` + `testdata/guided/privacy_copy.yaml`): asserts one intro sentence, the spelled-out `personally identifiable information (PII)` on first use, the truthful `project identity` / `git remote` / `maximum` framing, and forbids the old contradictory git-remote claim. - The existing fail-closed privacy-example checks are unchanged and still pass (each category renders exactly one demonstration that actually changes). - Updated golden guide fixtures (`framing.yaml`, `presentation_matrix.yaml`, `registry_parity.yaml`). The shorter guide now fits a common 80×24 terminal, so the paging-reveal viewport check moved to height 18 (where content still clips) to keep the same reveal assertion meaningful; the `personal data` reveal string is unchanged. **Mutation result:** reverting the copy fix (restoring the old intro/hints) makes `TestPrivacyGuideCopyContract` fail on the missing PII expansion, the missing project-identity framing, and the forbidden contradictory claim; restoring it passes. The viewport reveal remains self-guarding (fatal if the reveal is visible before paging). `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/tui/...`, and `go test ./internal/tui/... -count=1` are green. ## Verification - Tier: A. - Automated: the fixture-backed copy contract + the existing fail-closed and viewport checks. Part of epic #136. Closes #140. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

title: fix(tui): clarify kickstart selection step advance, keys, and folding (#139)
body: ## Problem The project/session selection step in `peasant kickstart` confused first-run users in four ways (issue #139): 1. No obvious way to advance — the advance action was `tab` labelled "next field", with no continue affordance. 2. A crowded footer listing the whole tree key set. 3. `a` "select all" appeared broken. 4. Every root opened fully expanded, so a first run was a wall of sessions. ## Fix - **Advance obvious.** The selection-step footer now shows a clear `tab: next step` affordance, so a first-time user sees how to progress without opening help. - **Pruned footer.** The footer on the selection step shows only the primary keys (`tab` advance, `shift+tab` previous when present, and `?` help); the full tree key set stays dispatchable and is listed under `?`. A new optional `keymap.FooterActionsProvider` lets an availability show a *subset* in the footer while help still derives from the complete `AvailableActions()`. Footer pruning steps aside while the filter is being typed or the preview pane is focused, so those modes still show their own keys. - **`a` select-all — root cause + fix.** On first run the default selection mode is `all`, so the forest opens **fully selected**. The old select-all was a *toggle*: with everything already checked it flipped to **clear**, so the very first press of "select all" deselected everything — the opposite of its label, which reads as "does nothing / broke it". Select-all is now **idempotent** (always selects, never clears) and is advertised/dispatchable only while something selectable is still unselected. Bulk clearing is intentionally not folded into the same key. - **Fold sessionless roots.** A project root with no already-imported or tracked session now opens **collapsed to its project line**; a root that carries imported or tracked work keeps its previous expansion. Implemented via a new `kit.Tree.CollapseInitial` seam plus a `settings.WithCollapseSessionlessRoots` option enabled on the kickstart selection field. ## Tests + mutation New fixture-backed test `TestSelectionStep_FirstRunUX` (`testdata/selection_ux.yaml`) drives the real mounted `kickstart.Program` on a genuine first run and asserts: the pruned `tab: next step` / `?: help` footer; the collapsed sessionless-root default; that an imported root opens expanded while others fold; and that `a` keeps a full selection selected (no hidden clear) and reselects after a deselect. Each of the four behaviors was mutation-checked by reverting the fix and confirming the matching case fails: - remove the collapse option → sessionless roots no longer fold (fails). - remove the compact-footer option → footer shows the full key set and the advance label reverts (fails). - revert select-all to toggle+old availability gate → `a` on a full selection clears it (fails). The kit `select-all-*` propagation fixture, the mounted touched-selection / retained-login / affordance fixtures, and the selection render goldens (both themes, in `internal/tui/kickstart` and `cmd/peasant`) were updated to the new footer and folding defaults. `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and `go test ./internal/tui/... ./cmd/peasant/...` are green. ## Verification (Tier A) — rendered captures ### First run — sessionless roots fold to the project line (dark) ``` ┌─ choose sessions to import ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ choose sessions to import privacy content license review & save │ │ │ │search: │ │harness ▸ ▸ [✓] github:acme/alpha all 2 ▸ [✓] github:acme/beta │harness: claude code │ │ claude code 2 │remote: github.com/acme/alpha │ │ │git directory: /fixtures/alpha │ │ │worktrees: 1 │ │ │ /fixtures/alpha │ │ │branches: 1 │ │ │ main │ │ │sessions: 1 │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │tab: next step ?: help │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ### First run — same, light theme ``` ┌─ choose sessions to import ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ choose sessions to import privacy content license review & save │ │ │ │search: │ │harness ▸ ▸ [✓] github:acme/alpha all 2 ▸ [✓] github:acme/beta │harness: claude code │ │ claude code 2 │remote: github.com/acme/alpha │ │ │git directory: /fixtures/alpha │ │ │worktrees: 1 │ │ │ /fixtures/alpha │ │ │branches: 1 │ │ │ main │ │ │sessions: 1 │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │tab: next step ?: help │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ### Imported root opens expanded, others fold (dark) ``` ┌─ choose sessions to import ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ choose sessions to import privacy content license review & save │ │ │ │search: │ │harness ▸ ▾ [✓] github:acme/alpha all 2 ▾ [✓] main │harness: claude code │ │ claude code 2 [✓] alpha session already imported │remote: github.com/acme/alpha │ │ ▸ [✓] github:acme/beta │git directory: /fixtures/alpha │ │ │worktrees: 1 │ │ │ /fixtures/alpha │ │ │branches: 1 │ │ │ main │ │ │sessions: 1 │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │tab: next step ?: help │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ## Judgment calls - **Select-all semantics.** The acceptance criterion says `a` must *select* the projection. Rather than keep a toggle (which clears on the default all-selected first run), `a` is now idempotent-select, and it is only offered while something is unselected. There is no dedicated bulk "clear all"; `space` still toggles a subtree. Flagging in case a separate clear-all is wanted. - **Collapse trigger** keys off "no imported or tracked session under the root" (`MetaIngested`/`MetaTracked`, both set before the decision runs). A returning user whose saved selection references a project but whose present branches don't intersect it (nothing matches → nothing tracked) will see that root fold; this is per the issue's literal rule. Affected mounted fixtures were updated to expand-then-navigate or assert the collapsed project row. Closes #139 Part of epic #136 --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. title: fix(tui): group kickstart final review into headed sections with a continue cue
body: ## Summary - The `settings.Flow` final review ("receipt") step listed the consent summary values/effects and changed-field sections as one flat run of lines, with no prominent cue that `enter` is the single commit action. - `internal/tui/settings/receipt.go`'s `renderReceipt` now bolds each group heading (`review your changes`, `your choices`, `when you confirm`, and each changed section title), blank-line separates the groups, bullets each item (`•`), and closes with a styled amber `press enter to continue` pill (`Styles.Selected`) so the primary action reads as obvious without opening help. - Effects/choices copy text is unchanged ("publish nothing", "import the selected transcripts", "save the visible choices", etc.) — only hierarchy and the progress cue changed. ## Verification - The guided-screenshots harness (`cmd/peasant-guided-screenshots`) does not currently mount `settings.Flow`'s receipt step, so this PR adds a focused printed-View test instead of extending that harness: `TestFlow_ReceiptGroupsChoicesAndEffectsWithAContinueCue` in `internal/tui/settings/flow_test.go`. It drives a real `Flow` to the receipt with a `ConsentSummary` attached, strips ANSI, and asserts: - `your choices` → its value → `when you confirm` → its effect → the changed-section heading → `press enter to continue` all appear in that reading order (never a flat block); - a real blank content row separates the `your choices` group from the `when you confirm` heading; - the continue-cue line still carries ANSI styling in the raw (unstripped) render, i.e. it's a distinct visual cue, not plain text. - Mutation-proven: stashed `receipt.go` back to the pre-fix render and confirmed the new test fails (no continue cue, no heading emphasis) before restoring the fix. - `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/tui/...`, and `go test ./internal/tui/... ./cmd/peasant/... -count=1` all pass. - Existing ANSI goldens for the receipt (`TestFlow_RenderGolden`'s `receipt-*`, `evidence-receipt-*`, and `viewport-receipt-error-bottom-*` cases) were regenerated via `-update` and diffed by eye — headings are now bold, items bulleted, and the amber continue pill is visible at realistic sizes (`80x24`+). At the smallest fixture (`40x8`) the cue can scroll below the fold, same as other receipt content already did before this change; the footer's persistent `enter: confirm` hint still covers that floor case. Part of epic #136 --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

title: feat(ingest): select canonical OpenCode projections
body: ## Summary - deduplicate mixed OpenCode JSON, legacy SQLite, and current SQLite sessions by raw session ID - select one deterministic canonical projection using current SQLite, then legacy SQLite, then JSON precedence - hydrate freshness only from the selected projection and preserve parent graphs, orphan content, tool pairing, and projection-specific ordering - verify all representation combinations through synthetic mounted harvest, real persistence, transcript detail conversion, and exact analytics assertions ## Safety OpenCode-managed databases remain read-only under the existing restrictive source boundary. Tests use synthetic temporary databases only; no live/default OpenCode data is accessed. ## Validation - focused canonical ingest and mounted command race tests with repeated runs - full ingest, fixture, API, transcript, store, and metrics race suites - `ast-grep scan --config sgconfig.yml .` - `make build` - `make check` - three-axis independent review with a final fix-free 0/0/0 round ## Round 2 A second review round raised further items. This push addresses the following, each with a fixture case and a mutation proof, and keeps the full ingest, transcript, api, and cmd/peasant race suites, `ast-grep`, and `make build` green: - Emit OpenCode parents before children in canonical discovery. Session IDs are time-descending, so a subagent sorted before its root by raw ID and the pipeline selection parent gate marked it unchanged in selected mode. Winners are now ordered parents-first by nearest-selected-ancestor depth, then by raw session ID. - Reject an unknown OpenCode provenance at canonical selection instead of letting `precedence()` rank it as zero and silently misorder a winner. - Report the zero time for an empty OpenCode freshness projection instead of the Unix epoch, so a caller can tell "no rows" from 1970 and fall back to the mtime floor. Both freshness reads share one decoder and check context after every statement; each statement stays a compile-time constant so the read-only SQL boundary guard still resolves the fixed set. - Route the OpenCode discovery and freshness failure diagnostics through `actionableOpenCodeDiagnostic`, registering both stages to the discovery-failed code so the hand-built diagnostic can no longer drift. The remaining second-review items (the freshness "changed" vs "active" clock split, per-session floor fallback, hybrid current-only selection, orphan and per-row source-decode tolerance, open-once source reuse, dangling-parent guard, and the related efficiency and fixture-coverage work) are not in this push and remain open. Closes #127 Closes #128 Closes #179 Part of #119. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled. ## Round 2, bundle A: freshness model and fixture infrastructure This bundle fixes the OpenCode freshness model and its fixture infrastructure. The changed clock is a per-session event clock (the newest row time of the selected projection combined with `session.time_updated` when the session has a usable clock); the database and WAL mtime floor applies only when a session has no usable clock. The active (staleness) gate uses the file and WAL mtime, independent of the changed clock. An in-place rewrite that moves no time column and no session clock is not detected as a change for a session that has a usable clock. Commits, in order: - `7f28bf6d` fix(ingest): model the OpenCode changed clock as one value per session. The clock is one optional value per session, so a session with no row or a null or zero clock takes the mtime-floor path and a row deletion for it is still seen. - `4a7c1192` perf(ingest): read OpenCode row freshness per table, not per session. One GROUP BY aggregate per present table per database replaces one aggregate per session, so freshness cost is bounded by table count, not session count. - `f6c0dab6` fix(ingest): classify OpenCode SQLite staleness on the file mtime. `DiscoveredSession.ActiveModTime` carries the file and WAL mtime for the staleness gate, independent of the changed clock; the CLI wiring active assertion is restored. - `3349ff14` test(ingest): cover the OpenCode mtime-floor and lagging-clock paths. A session clock mode in the fixture builder adds absent-clock and lagging-clock databases, with ingest and mounted harvest coverage of the floor and lag. - `384d2764` fix(ingest): skip only the session whose freshness floor read fails. A failed floor read skips only its own clockless session and names it, resolving the evidence index once per path, so sibling sessions still discover. - `dafe6a29` fix(ingest): keep an OpenCode winner whose freshness read fails. A winner whose row-freshness read fails falls back to the mtime floor and is kept, so a session with a readable representation is never silently dropped. The source-contract items (orphan tolerance, per-row degrade, hybrid current-only, open-once) are a later bundle and are not started here. ## Round 2, bundle B: source contract, open-once, and remaining efficiency This bundle fixes the source-contract, open-once, and remaining efficiency and reuse items. For a hybrid database, when the current projection discovers successfully, discovery returns current-only (the develop behaviour); the legacy tables are read only when current fails or is absent. Commits, in order: - `4a239bc0` perf(ingest): open each OpenCode database once per discovery. A supported database is opened once per Discover and the one source is reused for both enumerations, the session-record read, and freshness hydration; a shared open helper carries the nil-opener guard the session-record read lacked, and the schema probe stays a separate open. - `5a415fbc` fix(ingest): use current-only for a hybrid OpenCode database. When the current projection discovers successfully, the legacy tables are not read, so a session deleted from `session_message` is never resurrected from a stale legacy row. The canonical selection matrix and the real-store persistence corpus now split their hybrid database into a current database and a separate legacy database. - `d6938df5` fix(ingest): read OpenCode parent links without a clock column. Parent links are read whether or not `time_updated` exists; a session table with neither `parent_id` nor `time_updated` records a diagnostic. - `9e424f9e` fix(ingest): drop one bad OpenCode session row and keep the rest. An undecodable session row is dropped with a diagnostic and its cursor still advances, so one bad row no longer loses every session's parent link and clock. - `c8a3d1a1` fix(ingest): never fail an OpenCode session on a bad orphan part. An orphan part with BLOB data or an invalid identifier is dropped with the orphan-part-dropped warning instead of failing the session. - `4a37751d` fix(ingest): give OpenCode orphan parts a typed slot. The orphan is a typed message slot with no fabricated parent, so no spurious missing-parent warning; the managed legacy projection format is version 2 and version 1 stays readable; a cycle-broken parent link now records a diagnostic. - `9eca5c61` perf(ingest): skip the OpenCode session table with no candidates. Discovery returns before the session-record read when a database enumerated no sessions, and retains records only for the discovered ids. - `f43456c9` perf(ingest): detect OpenCode session columns once per source. The session table's column support is cached after the first page, so the pragma runs once per source rather than per page. - `c3c9c73c` refactor(ingest): share the OpenCode bounded-page validator and assembly. One shared bounded-page validator and one generic bounded-page helper replace the duplicated session-record validation and page assembly. - `df5a1518` perf(ingest): read a legacy OpenCode session's parts once. A single session-scoped part pass, partitioned in memory against the message-id set, replaces the per-message part read plus the correlated orphan scan. - `4f897dd2` fix(ingest): record one OpenCode freshness diagnostic per database. A database whose freshness read fails for every session records one diagnostic per outcome naming the sessions, not one per session. ## Round 2, bundle C - c9805753: state the ParentIndex contract for depth-0 entries (`ingest.Turn` doc, `docs/sessions.md`) and prove consumers key on `Depth`, not on `ParentIndex`: the overlay adoption loop is extracted to `contentOverlayFromEntries` and a fixture-driven test covers fold and overlay with mutation proofs. ## Round 3 Final-review fixes. Each correctness fix carries a mutation proof in its commit body. Commits are in review order. - `b7c86125` fix(ingest): carry the OpenCode message graph on ParentEntryID at depth 0. Depth-0 messages link through ParentEntryID like the Claude and Cursor indexers; ParentIndex stays nil at depth 0, so the schema wire contract is unchanged. - `191970f2` fix(ingest): fail an OpenCode session on an undecodable part for a present message. A bad part whose message is present fails the session; only a part whose message is absent stays a tolerated orphan, and a full page of dropped rows still advances the cursor. - `887eb10e` fix(ingest): ingest an OpenCode child as a root when its parent is not discovered. ParentUUID is set only when the parent is in the discovered set or the store; otherwise the child ingests as a root with a candidate diagnostic. - `4ca1024e` fix(ingest): bump the index version so changed OpenCode sessions re-index. - `222c13df` fix(ingest): surface OpenCode per-candidate discovery failures in the result. A supported candidate whose enumeration fails is reported through the pipeline result, so harvest and kickstart show the skipped database. - `529fe309` fix(ingest): close deferred OpenCode sources with a detached context, so an already-cancelled discovery context cannot leak the connection in the long-lived web process. - `c08c6e11` fix(ingest): type the raw identifiers of a dropped OpenCode part row, so the reader-surface contract guard no longer sees a bare-string identity on the surviving session-part read. - `de7718c3` fix(ingest): name only the pinned member of an OpenCode parent cycle, so a two-cycle and a three-cycle each record exactly one diagnostic. - `915a2020` refactor(ingest): remove the superseded OpenCode reader surface. The per-session freshness reads, the per-message legacy part read, the correlated orphan scan, their statements and helpers, and the version 1 orphan marker are deleted; the reader inventory and allowed-statement counts are updated. - `c0a47f7a` fix(ingest): report one drop per bad OpenCode session row. The session-record cursor advances past the last observed identifier after a drop, so a bad tail row is not re-fetched and counted twice. - `cb895473` test(peasant): move the OpenCode session-clock mount cases to a testdata fixture with an embed loader and a typed mutation field. - `9edc3c75` test(peasant): assert the depth-0 OpenCode graph on ParentEntryID, aligning the mounted canonical persistence test with the depth-0 contract. ### Re-materialization note Bumping the index version re-indexes already-indexed OpenCode sessions, so they pick up the ParentEntryID links and the orphan-part system entries. Current-SQLite managed artifacts materialized before this branch carry no parentID, so a re-index alone cannot link them; those artifacts need re-materialization (a fresh harvest of the source) to gain the depth-0 parent links, not only a re-index. ## Round 4: hybrid union restored A hybrid OpenCode database carries both the legacy `message`/`part` tables and the current `session_message` projection. An earlier round narrowed hybrid discovery to the current projection alone whenever it read successfully, so every session that lived only in the legacy tables became invisible. On the maintainer's real store the legacy tables hold 4,592 distinct sessions while the current projection holds 47, so discovery dropped almost everything. This round restores the union and handles deletions precisely: - **Union both projections.** Discovery enumerates both projections again and canonical selection keeps one per session, current outranking legacy. A session in both is a current winner; a session only in the legacy tables is a legacy winner. - **Deleted sessions.** The session table is OpenCode's authoritative session list. When it carries the changed clock (the real OpenCode shape), a discovered session with no row there was deleted, so it is skipped with a diagnostic rather than resurrected from its historical rows. A session table without the clock column fails safe and keeps every discovered session. - **Diagnostics match their outcome.** The dangling-parent diagnostic (sessions ingested as roots) and the freshness floor-fallback diagnostic no longer report that sessions were "skipped"; each carries a meaning and remediation that match what happened. ### Real-store dry run (read-only) `peasant harvest --dry-run --source-provider opencode --source-path ~/.local/share/opencode` - Before: `peasant harvest: 231 sessions` - After: `peasant harvest: 4592 sessions (0 new, 21 updated, 4571 unchanged, 0 errors), 0 active (debounced)` No skipped-candidate diagnostics and no genuine deleted sessions on this store. The dangling-parent warning for `ses_0f0963c0cffe7CuTb86VkUA1Sy`'s children is gone because that parent (69 legacy rows) is now discovered. The sole discovery warning is the freshness floor-fallback for the legacy sessions, which are all still discovered. ## Round 5: clock-first freshness Freshness hydration read the per-table row aggregates (`MAX(MAX(time_created,time_updated)) ... GROUP BY session_id` over `message`, `part`, and `session_message`) for every SQLite database, whether or not the selected sessions carried a usable session clock. On a very large legacy store the `part` aggregate exceeds the per-statement query timeout, so the batch read failed and every legacy session on that database was reported as having fallen back to the file and write-ahead-log mtime floor, even though each one had a `session.time_updated` clock that already reports its changed time. With the floor in force, any later OpenCode write reclassified those sessions as updated. - **Clock-first read.** The row aggregate is now read for a database only when at least one selected session on it has no usable clock. A session that has a clock uses the clock as its changed time and the file and WAL mtime as its active time, so a database whose sessions all carry a clock runs no freshness aggregate at all and never scans a large `message`, `part`, or `session_message` table. Clockless sessions keep the existing row-aggregate and floor path. - **A failed read spares clock-bearing sessions.** Because a clock-bearing session never reads the aggregate, a failed aggregate read (timeout or busy) can no longer demote it. Only the clockless sessions of a database fall to the floor, and only they are named in the floor-fallback diagnostic. ### Real-store dry run (read-only) `make build && ./bin/peasant harvest --dry-run --source-provider opencode --source-path ~/.local/share/opencode` - Before (tip `26fe2ede`): `peasant harvest: 4592 sessions (0 new, 21 updated, 4571 unchanged, 0 errors), 0 active (debounced) [1m7s]`, with one WARN reporting 4545 sessions fell back to the database and WAL mtime floor. - After: `peasant harvest: 4592 sessions (0 new, 0 updated, 4592 unchanged, 0 errors), 0 active (debounced) [59.8s]`, with no freshness floor-fallback WARN (stderr is empty). Same 4592 sessions, no floor-fallback warning, and the run is not slower. The 21 previously-updated sessions were spurious floor-driven reclassifications: with the clock as the changed time, the unchanged sessions read older than their stored ingest time and stay unchanged. ## Round 6: session attribution and the column allowlist SQLite-discovered OpenCode sessions never set the working directory, title, or creation time on the discovered session, while the JSON path did. Kickstart groups projects by the git remote resolved from the session's working directory, so a session with no working directory fell into a name-keyed catch-all instead of its project. On the maintainer's real store, 2,118 of 4,592 discovered sessions have a session directory under `/home/minttea/dev/peasant-labs`, and none grouped under that project. This round reads the working directory, title, and creation time from the session row at discovery, so those sessions group under the project their directory resolves to. ### Read-only guard change (maintainer authorized) The discovery-time session read is bounded by a read-only SQL guard. The maintainer, who designed this guard, authorized two changes to it for the session table: (1) convert the forbidden-column token denylist into an allowlist of readable session columns, and (2) include `directory` and `title` in that allowlist. The approved readable set for the session table is exactly `id, parent_id, time_updated, time_created, directory, title`. Every other session column (including `share_url`, `summary`, `metadata`, `revert`, `permission`, `slug`, `version`, `workspace_id`, `path`, `agent`, `model`, `cost`, and the token and summary columns) stays unreadable, enforced by the allowlist. The authorizer, the fixed statement set, and the other tables' guards are unchanged. Rationale: `directory` and `title` already reach Peasant through the JSON layout at discovery and through message data at materialization, so the discovery-time guard was blocking what ingest already carries. The allowlist fails closed and is mutation-proven: a session statement that adds `share_url` projects a column outside the allowlist and is rejected. ### Real-store acceptance (read-only) A throwaway probe constructed the OpenCode adapter exactly as production does (read-only source opener) and ran discovery against `/home/minttea/.local/share/opencode`, strictly read-only, then was deleted: - `total_discovered=4592` - `non_empty_cwd=4592` - `cwd_under_peasant_labs=2118` - `non_empty_title=4592` All 4,592 discovered sessions now carry their working directory and title, and the 2,118 sessions under `/home/minttea/dev/peasant-labs` now group under that project instead of the catch-all. ## Round 7: allowlist extension (folds #179) Round 6 read the working directory, title, and creation time from the session row. Round 7 extends the same fail-closed read to the rest of the Claude-parity attribution, guided by a read-only census of the maintainer's store and authorized by the maintainer on 2026-08-24 (recorded in #179). - **Allowlist extension.** The session-table allowlist grows to sixteen columns, adding `agent`, the five token aggregates, `cost`, `version`, `slug`, and `revert`. Four new per-table allowlists govern `project` (`id, worktree, vcs, name`), `project_directory` (`project_id, directory, type`), `workspace` (all eight columns), and `event_sequence` (`aggregate_id, seq, owner_id`). Each table carries a can-go-red proof: a statement projecting a column outside its set is rejected, and the row guard refuses a vacuous proof. `event.data`, `event.type`, `session.share_url`, `session.summary_*`, `session.metadata`, `session.permission`, and the `session_share`/`permission`/`credential`/`account*`/`control_account` tables stay unreadable. SINGLE-SHOT ses_00f3467e4ffeXd5GIO7BNOWRGI elapsed=41ms turns=23 notice="" SINGLE-SHOT ses_ff76065e0ffe7bTgKI2KkAF1Cz elapsed=2ms turns=4 notice="" ``` After, the two-step read: ``` FIRST PAGE ses_06a7c4dfeffePm4KcVV5bt9yDR elapsed=456ms turns=34 more=true notice="" FULL READ ses_06a7c4dfeffePm4KcVV5bt9yDR elapsed=7.208s turns=121 notice="preview shows the first 26 MiB of this 2232 MiB session (432 of 16,072 rows). the full session ingests normally. this bound applies to the preview only." MATCH ses_06a7c4dfeffePm4KcVV5bt9yDR full read is turn-for-turn and note-for-note the single-shot result FIRST PAGE ses_00f3467e4ffeXd5GIO7BNOWRGI elapsed=8ms turns=15 more=true notice="" FULL READ ses_00f3467e4ffeXd5GIO7BNOWRGI elapsed=40ms turns=23 notice="" MATCH ses_00f3467e4ffeXd5GIO7BNOWRGI full read is turn-for-turn and note-for-note the single-shot result FIRST PAGE ses_ff76065e0ffe7bTgKI2KkAF1Cz elapsed=1ms turns=4 more=false notice="" SINGLE-STEP ses_ff76065e0ffe7bTgKI2KkAF1Cz the slice is the whole session; no full read runs FULL READ ses_ff76065e0ffe7bTgKI2KkAF1Cz elapsed=0s turns=4 notice="" MATCH ses_ff76065e0ffe7bTgKI2KkAF1Cz full read is turn-for-turn and note-for-note the single-shot result ``` First paint on the 2.2 GiB session drops from 7.354 s to 456 ms, and the whole read behind it is turn-for-turn and note-for-note what the single read produced. **One deviation, with evidence.** The brief named `ses_00f3467e4ffeXd5GIO7BNOWRGI` as the single-step example. Its payload is 603 KiB, so at a 64 KiB bound it takes the two-step path (8 ms + 40 ms, both imperceptible). Sizing the bound to 1 MiB so it would fit in one read costs the 2.2 GiB session 1.32 s instead of 0.44 s of first paint, which fails the "well under one second" requirement. The single-step path is demonstrated above on `ses_ff76065e0ffe7bTgKI2KkAF1Cz` (2.1 KiB payload) instead. ### Tests Fixture-driven, required-NAME manifests, no count guards. `internal/tui/kit/testdata/previewsplit_progressive.yaml` — the pane, both steps, over a source whose two bodies carry different line prefixes so every assertion names which one is on screen: | mutation | red case | |---|---| | the swap never runs | 4 cases | | the swap always returns to the top | `a-scrolled-swap-keeps-the-offset-the-reader-is-at` | | the swap is treated as a fresh load | `a-scrolled-swap-keeps-the-offset-the-reader-is-at` | | the stale guard is gone | `a-highlight-change-discards-the-whole-body-still-being-read` | | the pane never says it is still reading | 4 cases | | a first read that is already whole still triggers a second | `a-plain-body-source-keeps-its-single-step-load`, `a-progressive-source-with-nothing-more-never-reads-the-whole-body` | | the progressive capability is ignored | 5 cases | | delete a required fixture case row | named by the required-name manifest | `internal/tui/kickstart/testdata/source_preview_two_step.yaml` — the reader and the pane against a real synthetic provider database: | mutation | red case | |---|---| | the leading slice is cached | 3 cases | | the first-page read never reports that more follows | 3 cases | | the note is attached to the slice too | `the-note-of-a-two-step-read-describes-the-whole-read-not-the-slice` | | the pane ignores the first-page reader | `the-note-of-a-two-step-read-describes-the-whole-read-not-the-slice` | | delete a required fixture case row | named by the required-name manifest | The cache rule is proven DIRECTLY rather than by comparing turn counts, which a session whose slice already holds every turn cannot show: a fresh reader takes the slice, the provider database is removed, and the whole read must then FAIL (the slice was never cached) while a session read whole in one step must still answer. The note rule supplies the note unconditionally, for the slice as much as for the whole body, so the PANE is the only thing that can keep it off the slice. Golden `View()` coverage extends the existing kit render matrix with a `previewsplit-loading-the-rest` component: both themes, three sizes. ``` go test ./internal/tui/kit/ ok EXIT=0 go test ./internal/tui/... ./internal/defaults/ ok EXIT=0 make check EXIT=0 ``` --- ## Scroll-triggered incremental loading in the kickstart preview The preview of a very long OpenCode session used to END at the byte bound its first read used: the reader reached the bottom and the transcript simply stopped, under a sentence explaining that the rest was left out. On the real 2.2 GiB session that is 121 turns out of 2,232 MiB, and no way forward. Scrolling to the bottom of the pane now loads the next chunk and appends it, so the preview keeps extending for as long as the reader keeps reading. The same session reaches **883 turns and 665 MiB after twenty scrolls, all of them drawn on screen** — the pane grows from 3,467 to 17,787 rendered lines — with nothing shown twice. > **Correction, added later in this branch.** This paragraph originally claimed > 883 turns after twenty scrolls WITHOUT saying that the figure counted turns > LOADED rather than turns DRAWN. At the time it was written those are not the > same number: only the first 200 were drawn, and the pane summarized the rest > away, so past turn 200 scrolling changed nothing on screen. The sentence above > now quotes rendered lines, which is what a reader actually sees. The defect, > its fix, and the measurements are in "The pane was loading turns it never > drew" below. ### The continuation `ingest.TranscriptSliceCursor` is a VALUE, not a handle. It carries the source's own keyset positions and the running totals the pane's sentence quotes, so each slice re-opens the provider database read-only, seeks by cursor, reads one budget-sized slice, and closes. **Nothing stays open while the reader merely looks at the pane**, and the whole-session payload size is measured once and carried rather than re-summed per scroll. No new SQL was needed: the paged message and part reads already accept an `After` cursor, and their cursor types already had exported constructors. The statement set, the authorizer, and the read-only mode are untouched. ### The seam **A slice ends on a MESSAGE boundary**, which is what lets the caller simply APPEND one slice's turns to the previous slice's: - The message pass is a strictly forward keyset walk, so a message enters exactly one slice. - The part pass attaches a part only to a message in the CURRENT window. When the budget runs out part-way through a message it drains that message's remaining parts and stops at the first part of the NEXT one; window messages past the cut are dropped from the slice and read again by the next one. They were never emitted, so nothing is shown twice. - A part whose message lies past the window stops the pass WITHOUT being consumed, so the next slice picks it up rather than losing it. A part that blocks two slices in a row belongs to an already-emitted message and is stepped over, which guarantees progress. - A part with no message in memory is treated as an orphan ONLY when the read covered the whole session from the start. On a continuation an unattached part almost always belongs to an adjacent slice, and synthesizing a root for it there would invent a turn the session never held. A resumable read charges its two passes separately. A single legacy message row reaches 25 MiB on the real store, which alone exceeds a sensible slice budget, so a shared counter left every continuation able to afford ONE message and turned the 2.2 GiB session into thousands of slices. One-shot bounded and first-page reads keep their existing shared bound and their existing results. ### The pane `kit.ContinuableBodySource` is a new OPTIONAL capability beside the two-step one. A source reports whether the body on screen has more behind it and hands back the WHOLE preview extended when asked. Because an extension only ever appends, the pane keeps the reader's scroll offset and **the line under their eye does not move**. - The request goes out **three rows** before the end (`previewContinueThresholdLines`), so the chunk is usually there before the reader arrives. - It carries the same load sequence as the body it extends, so moving the highlight discards one still in flight. - While it runs the pane says `loading more...` on a line at the BOTTOM of the body. The row that line occupies is RESERVED, blank, from the moment the preview can be continued at all, so firing the request cannot shift the view. A source that cannot be continued, a file transcript, and a session read whole keep their existing behavior untouched. ### The sentence above the turns is now live It restates itself after every chunk so its figures follow what is actually on screen, and it names the way forward: ``` showing the first 26 MiB of this 2232 MiB session. scroll to the bottom to load more. the full session ingests normally. ``` It replaces the fixed note, whose closing clause about the bound applying to the preview only said less than the scroll affordance now does, and it disappears entirely once the session has nothing more behind it. ### Real-store acceptance Read-only, against `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (423 GB), through the real `kickstart.SourceTurns` the mounted pane uses. **The 2.2 GiB legacy session `ses_06a7c4dfeffePm4KcVV5bt9yDR`**, default bounds: ``` FIRST PAGE 446ms turns=34 more=true FIRST READ 4.045s turns=121 more=true note: showing the first 26 MiB of this 2232 MiB session. scroll to the bottom to load more. the full session ingests normally. SCROLL 1 1.802s new=6 total=127 more=true note: showing the first 57 MiB of this 2232 MiB session. scroll to the bottom to load more. the full session ingests normally. SCROLL 2 1.766s new=23 total=150 more=true note: showing the first 87 MiB of this 2232 MiB session. scroll to the bottom to load more. the full session ingests normally. SCROLL 3 1.648s new=27 total=177 more=true note: showing the first 118 MiB of this 2232 MiB session. scroll to the bottom to load more. the full session ingests normally. SCROLL 4 1.52s new=14 total=191 more=true note: showing the first 149 MiB of this 2232 MiB session. scroll to the bottom to load more. the full session ingests normally. SCROLL 5 1.351s new=9 total=200 more=true note: showing the first 179 MiB of this 2232 MiB session. scroll to the bottom to load more. the full session ingests normally. SCROLL 6 1.337s new=19 total=219 more=true note: showing the first 211 MiB of this 2232 MiB session. scroll to the bottom to load more. the full session ingests normally. FINAL: 219 turns retained ``` Continued to twenty scrolls, no failure and no repeat: ``` SCROLL 12 2.489s new=103 total=651 more=true SCROLL 15 3.403s new=16 total=697 more=true SCROLL 20 1.778s new=38 total=883 more=true note: showing the first 665 MiB of this 2232 MiB session. scroll to the bottom to load more. the full session ingests normally. FINAL: 883 turns retained ``` The first read is unchanged from before this change (121 turns, 26 MiB), so the starting point the reader sees is the same; scrolling is purely additive. Each scroll costs **1.3 to 3.4 seconds** and adds anywhere from 6 to 144 turns. **Termination**, on the 226 KiB session `ses_0002794d3ffeL3LvlX1bGAZx3e` at 32 KiB bounds, because exhausting the 2.2 GiB one is impractical: ``` FIRST PAGE 31ms turns=13 more=true FIRST READ 16ms turns=3 more=true note: showing the first 112 KiB of this 220 KiB session. scroll to the bottom to load more. the full session ingests normally. SCROLL 1 12ms new=3 total=6 more=true note: showing the first 148 KiB of this 220 KiB session. scroll to the bottom to load more. the full session ingests normally. SCROLL 2 11ms new=2 total=8 more=true note: showing the first 187 KiB of this 220 KiB session. scroll to the bottom to load more. the full session ingests normally. SCROLL 3 10ms new=6 total=14 more=false note: (no sentence: the preview holds the whole session) SESSION EXHAUSTED: the pane offers no more and shows no sentence FINAL: 14 turns retained ``` The 14 turns it lands on are exactly what an unbounded whole-session read of that session produces. **No turn is repeated at any seam.** Keyed on role, timestamp, and content across all twenty scrolls of the 2.2 GiB session: zero. Keyed on role and content alone there is one hit at scroll 6, which is a prompt the operator genuinely typed twice in that session: ``` repeated turn: role=user ts=2026-07-21 01:26:18.006 -0700 PDT len=100 content="Continue if you have next steps, or stop and ask for clarification if you are unsure how to proceed." ``` ### Two real-store findings worth recording **Part identifiers do not invert on real data.** The seam rules depend on a part of a later message sorting after a part of an earlier one. Measured directly: **4,559 consecutive part rows of the 2.2 GiB session, zero inversions**. OpenCode mints part identifiers as a message streams, so this is structural rather than lucky. The synthetic fixtures whose identifiers are hand-written words CAN invert, and one case exists for exactly that: it declares by NAME the single row the scrolled preview leaves out, rather than claiming a completeness the read cannot have on such data. The read never shows a turn twice and never invents one, on any ordering. **One part row of that session cannot be read inside the source's 5s query deadline.** Stepping the part table one row at a time, row 4,560 fails reproducibly at page size 16, at page size 1, and on three warm retries. This is a property of the data, not of this change, and it is a hard ceiling on how far ANY read of that session can walk the part table from the beginning. The twenty scrolls above did not reach it, because the message-window pass advances differently. A continuation that does hit it returns an actionable error the pane renders in place, and the pane stops offering more rather than retrying. Worth a follow-up: the source could pre-check `LENGTH(data)` and report an unreadably large row rather than timing out on it. ### Tests All cases live in `testdata/*.yaml` fixtures with `//go:embed`, guarded by required-NAME manifests. No new integer count guards. | fixture | covers | |---|---| | `internal/ingest/testdata/opencode_slice_continuation.yaml` | no message emitted by two slices; nothing invented; nothing lost; the chain terminates; the cursor's counts never shrink or exceed the session totals | | `internal/tui/kit/testdata/previewsplit_continue.yaml` | the threshold triggers a request; exactly the threshold triggers without reaching the end; short of it triggers nothing; a second scroll in flight does not ask twice; stale discard on highlight change; the appended chunk keeps the reader's line; the last chunk ends the offers | | `internal/tui/kickstart/testdata/source_preview_scroll.yaml` | every continuation appends; nothing the reader can see appears twice; the chain ends; the sentence follows the screen and disappears at the end | Two source fixtures were added: `legacy-scrollable-session` (part identifiers minted in message order, one message of three parts, so a small budget both slices it and exercises the drain) and `legacy-out-of-order-parts` (identifiers that sort against their messages, which is what exercises the step-over). **Mutation-proving.** Nineteen mutations were checked across the three layers and every one goes red: - ingest: dropping the message-boundary drain; skipping an out-of-window part instead of retrying it; treating a continuation's unattached part as an orphan; keeping the window messages past the cut; leaving the message cursor ahead of the cut; both directions of the step-over guard. - kit: both directions of the threshold; allowing a second in-flight request; resetting the scroll on a continuation; never learning a body is continuable; never drawing the label; dropping the reserved row. - kickstart: replacing instead of appending; dropping the appended turns; continuing from the start of the session; writing the sentence once; leaving it up after exhaustion; reporting more when there is none. Golden `View()` coverage extends the kit render matrix with two components, both themes, three sizes: `previewsplit-loading-more` and `previewsplit-more-to-load`. Both are captured SCROLLED TO THE END, where the state's chrome lives; the pair shows the reader's first row unchanged across the two, which is the scroll-stability claim as a picture. ``` go test ./internal/ingest/... ok EXIT=0 go test ./internal/tui/kit/ ok EXIT=0 go test ./internal/tui/kickstart/ ok EXIT=0 make check EXIT=0 ``` ### Note for reviewers `internal/tui/kit/testdata/render_matrix.yaml` carries a pre-existing `expectedCaseCount` / `expectedComponentCount` pair. Adding two components required bumping both. That is exactly the churn the no-count-guard rule describes, and the fixture already lists its components by name; replacing the counts with that manifest is a clean follow-up, kept out of this change. --- ## The pane was loading turns it never drew A defect in the scroll-paging above, found by rendering the ACTUAL preview body instead of counting the turns behind it. Every gate on that work was green while the feature stopped working past turn 200. `transcriptview.MaxRenderedTurns = 200` caps what one `Render` lays out and replaces the rest with `(N more turns not shown here)`. The preview renders through it. So past that point the reader scrolled, the loader worked, and the transcript on screen did not change. Measured on the 2.2 GiB session at width 100: ``` FIRST READ turns=121 renderedLines=3467 SCROLL 5 turns=200 renderedLines=4715 SCROLL 6 turns=219 renderedLines=4717 lastLine="(19 more turns not shown here)" SCROLL 20 turns=883 renderedLines=4717 lastLine="(683 more turns not shown here)" ``` The body froze at 4,717 lines. **683 turns loaded and never shown.** Nothing caught it because the kit cases use a synthetic lines-body and the kickstart cases assert turn slices — neither goes through the real renderer. ### Why the bound exists, and why it does not apply here It caps the cost of laying out turns NOBODY ASKED FOR: a caller hands over a whole recorded session and the first draw does more work than a person reads before scrolling. A scrolled preview inverts that — its turns are there because the reader scrolled for them. So `Renderer` gains an opt-in `UnboundedDocument`, and the preview uses it for a session it can extend or has extended. **A session handed over whole keeps the standing bound and its notice**, so the mounted session viewer and every other caller are unchanged. The choice is per session: a store-backed session in the same list stays bounded while a harness-read one beside it is not. ### The cache cliff underneath it Lifting the bound exposed a second failure. The per-turn cache is dropped WHOLE when exceeded, so a working set one entry past `maxCachedTurns = 512` clears the map part-way through every draw and every re-draw pays a fully cold render: ``` re-draw same width 200 turns 2ms 363 turns 211ms 883 turns 563ms ← on every frame, so every keystroke ``` The ceiling now follows the largest document actually drawn, rising only for a caller that has already chosen to hold that many turns, so the memory it allows stays proportional to what the reader asked to see. A bounded document sits below the starting ceiling and never moves it. ### The cache ceiling, measured at the depths a reader reaches Asked for explicitly in review, so that lifting the turn cap could not hide a render cliff behind it. The number that decides whether the surface is usable is the **re-draw**: the pane re-renders on every keystroke, so that is what a reader pays per key. Synthetic turns of realistic size, one renderer per depth, at width 100. **Without the ceiling fix** — the cliff: | loaded turns | cold draw | re-draw | re-draw after a resize | |---|---|---|---| | 200 | 110ms | 0ms | 0ms | | 500 | 266ms | 1ms | **269ms** | | 900 | 469ms | **468ms** | **457ms** | At 900 turns every keystroke costs 468ms. Note the 500-turn row: the settled width alone still fits under `maxCachedTurns = 512`, so the cliff only appears once a RESIZE brings a second width into play — which makes it reachable much earlier than the raw turn count suggests. **With the ceiling fix:** | loaded turns | cold draw | re-draw | re-draw after a resize | |---|---|---|---| | 200 | 110ms | 0ms | 0ms | | 500 | 270ms | 1ms | 1ms | | 900 | 473ms | 1ms | 1ms | Re-draw stays at 0-1ms at every depth. Cold draw still grows with the document, but that is paid once when the content arrives, and in real scrolling only the NEW turns are cold — measured at 3 to 70ms per scroll on the real session. **The fix is scoped, not global.** A bounded document caps at `MaxRenderedTurns = 200`, so `200 x cacheWidthsKeptWarm` sits below the starting ceiling and can never move it. Measured on the same run, a bounded document at all three depths: cold ~105ms regardless of how many turns it was handed, re-draw 0ms, still capped at 200 drawn. `TestTurnCache_ABoundedDocumentKeepsTheStartingCeiling` asserts the ceiling does not move, and goes red if it does. No render window was needed: per-draw cost is not interactive-hostile at any reachable depth once the ceiling follows the document. ### After both fixes, same session ``` FIRST READ turns=121 renderedLines=3467 render=168ms re-draw=2ms SCROLL 5 turns=200 renderedLines=4715 render=5ms re-draw=2ms SCROLL 6 turns=219 renderedLines=5130 render=14ms re-draw=2ms SCROLL 10 turns=516 renderedLines=10627 render=31ms re-draw=5ms SCROLL 15 turns=697 renderedLines=14727 render=36ms re-draw=7ms SCROLL 20 turns=883 renderedLines=17787 render=16ms re-draw=7ms ``` The drawn body grows monotonically, 3,467 to 17,787 lines. A scroll costs 3 to 70ms to draw and a re-draw at 883 turns is 7ms. ### Tests New fixtures assert the RENDERED BODY, which is what the passing gates failed to do: `internal/tui/transcriptview/testdata/draw_bound.yaml` (a handed-over transcript draws its bound and says what it left out; a scrolled one draws every turn) and `internal/tui/kickstart/testdata/preview_growth.yaml` (the drawn body grows on every scroll past the bound; an exhausted preview does not take the bound back; a handed-over session keeps it). Two cache cases pin the ceiling rising for a scrolled document and NOT rising for a bounded one. Six mutations, all red, including a faithful reproduction of the original defect (the preview reverting to the bounded document). --- ## The same paging for file-origin harnesses Claude, Codex and Cursor transcripts are JSONL files, and the preview read every byte of one, indexed every entry, and folded every turn before anything appeared. The largest here is **290 MiB**. It now paints a leading slice at once and takes the rest as the reader scrolls, through the same pane seam and the same kickstart wiring as the OpenCode path — nothing harness-specific was added to `previewsplit.go`. **Bounds:** the OpenCode preview's own constants, not new numbers, per the user ruling. No new magic values were introduced; the shared fields carry a comment saying the mirroring is deliberate. ### The seam, and what actually solves it Lines never split — the read is a byte range extended to the last newline. But that is not what makes it correct, and the code says so: - **A turn straddles lines.** A tool call and the result that answers it are two records joined by a call identifier. Folding one slice at a time would leave the call resultless and drop the output entirely, because an orphan result is suppressed rather than drawn. - **Every file indexer carries state across records** while it parses — which calls asked the user a question, which parent a record belongs to. A parse starting mid-file would classify records differently from the whole-file read. So the preview keeps the raw bytes it has read and **re-parses and re-folds the whole accumulated prefix** on every slice. Re-reading is what a slice avoids; re-parsing what is already in memory is cheap by comparison, and holding those bytes costs no more than the whole-file read it replaces. Given that, the newline trimming is a cleanliness and speed measure rather than a correctness one — a slice ending mid-line would be completed by the next and the final result would be identical. Its comments say exactly that rather than claiming more. **Line-orientation is now declared, not assumed.** An indexer implements `LineOrientedTranscriptIndexer` to say one record occupies one line. A format that does not keeps the whole-file read — as does a filesystem that cannot read a byte range, and a transcript inside its first-page bound, which is read exactly once as it always was. ### Real-store acceptance **Equivalence** is the gate that matters: read a real transcript BOTH ways and compare turn for turn, including each turn's tool calls and their output. | transcript | size | lines | slices | result | |---|---|---|---|---| | Claude `504ced8a` | 10.19 MiB | 6,309 | 168 | identical | | Claude `f6cb7389` | 13.24 MiB | 6,286 | 234 | identical | | Claude `338298d1` | 10.05 MiB | 5,521 | 170 | identical | | Codex rollout | 54.24 MiB | 32,098 | 929 | identical | | Cursor transcript | 0.36 MiB | 327 | 5 | identical | Each Claude case was also run at 4 KiB and 1 MiB budgets (2,543 and 13 slices) — identical every time. **Codex and Cursor transcripts are JSONL and use the same reader**, so both are wired; no harness needed to be left on the one-shot path. **Largest real Claude JSONL, 290 MiB:** ``` FILE .../54ae362e-.../subagents/agent-a814f85.jsonl 290.5 MiB (304620516 bytes) FIRST PAINT 1ms drawnLines=161 more=true FIRST READ 646ms turns=20 drawnLines=164 more=true note: showing the first 62 MiB of this 290 MiB session. scroll to the bottom to load more. the full session ingests normally. SCROLL 1 661ms new=0 turns=20 drawnLines=164 more=true SCROLL 2 722ms new=0 turns=20 drawnLines=164 more=true SCROLL 3 707ms new=0 turns=20 drawnLines=164 more=true ``` First paint **1ms**, well under the required second. This file is 131 lines averaging 2.3 MB each, so a chunk is two or three enormous tool results that fold into turns already on screen; `MaxToolResultLines = 8` then caps what each adds. The content is loaded and joined correctly — it just does not lengthen the pane. See the follow-up below. **120 MiB main session, scrolled to exhaustion:** ``` FIRST PAINT 3ms drawnLines=173 more=true FIRST READ 1.125s turns=716 drawnLines=8709 more=true SCROLL 1 876ms new=0 turns=716 drawnLines=8709 more=true SCROLL 4 966ms new=0 turns=716 drawnLines=8727 more=true SCROLL 6 1.048s new=0 turns=716 drawnLines=8754 more=true SCROLL 7 1.183s new=141 turns=857 drawnLines=10701 more=true SCROLL 8 1.086s new=19 turns=876 drawnLines=11361 more=false note: (no sentence: the preview holds the whole transcript) EXHAUSTED: the pane offers no more and shows no sentence ``` Terminates honestly. Scrolls 4-6 grow the body without adding turns — that is the seam design working, later tool results joining calls already on screen. Cost is **0.7 to 1.2s per scroll** on a file this size, because each scroll re-parses the accumulated prefix; that is the price of matching the whole-file read exactly, and it is comparable to the OpenCode path's 1.3-3.4s. **Small session, single-phase:** ``` 0.0 MiB (22636 bytes) FIRST PAINT 1ms drawnLines=440 more=false FIRST READ 0s turns=8 drawnLines=440 more=false note: (no sentence: the preview holds the whole transcript) EXHAUSTED: the pane offers no more and shows no sentence ``` Read once, no second phase, no sentence — identical to today. ### Tests `internal/ingest/testdata/file_slice.yaml` pins the slicer: every slice ends on a line, the slices rebuild the file byte for byte, the read terminates, an oversized line arrives whole, and a file with no trailing newline still ends cleanly. `internal/tui/kickstart/testdata/file_slice_preview.yaml` pins equivalence on fixture transcripts whose tool results land in later slices, carrying unmistakable output markers so an empty-versus-empty comparison cannot pass. **Mutation-proving, reported honestly.** Of eight mutations checked on this work, six go red — including the per-slice parse (which loses tool output), a trim that drops the newline, an unchased oversized line, and a cursor that does not advance. **Two do not, and they are behaviourally equivalent rather than test gaps**: removing the last-newline fast path, and removing the end-of-file fast path. Both fall through to the forward-read that produces the same bytes by another route. They are performance guards, and the code now says so instead of claiming they hold the seam together. ``` go test ./internal/ingest/... ok EXIT=0 go test ./internal/tui/... ok EXIT=0 make check EXIT=0 ``` ### Follow-ups this surfaced 1. **A scroll can load megabytes and add no visible lines** when a chunk is one huge tool result, because `MaxToolResultLines = 8` caps what a result draws. Correct, but it reads as an unresponsive pane. Worth deciding whether a continuation should keep reading until it adds rendered content. 2. **`render_matrix.yaml` still carries `expectedCaseCount` / `expectedComponentCount`**, which had to be bumped again for the two new components. The fixture already lists components by name; replacing the counts with that manifest is a clean follow-up, kept out of this change.

title: fix(ingest): restore OpenCode v2 session ingestion
body: ## Summary Restore ingestion of OpenCode conversations after the native v2 store migration. - Discover live sessions from both supported `session_v2` and legacy `session` tables. Prefer V2 metadata for shared IDs and use legacy metadata for V1-only IDs, including parent links and freshness. Missing V2 identity alone never proves deletion. - Accept native `session_message` payloads with column-owned identity. Decode native user, assistant, tool, shell, attachment, and compaction variants while retaining historical formats and strict invalid-data checks. - Record v2 catalog evidence and distinguish unsupported metadata, incomplete reads, and absence of live records in diagnostics. Do not claim deletion history from missing records. - Add named YAML fixtures and a built-Peasant CLI regression for first ingest, unchanged repeat ingest, changed source input, persisted results, and source DB/sidecar preservation. The child CLI matches the enclosing suite's race mode, retaining race instrumentation in local/release race runs and supporting nonrace/CGO-disabled CI. - Use `opencode_v2` file and format names. body:
## Summary

- Persist complete recorded text in SQLite and derive bounded prose previews from it. Preserve complete tool inputs, outputs, and structured entry metadata.
- Use one verified full-content database reader for session detail, export, share scans, and publication. Redact complete content before constructing either outgoing multipart part.
- Verify complete reads once within one SQLite snapshot. Bind full content to the same metadata/index capture revision; readiness lists check eligibility without loading transcript bodies.
- Use shared 256 KiB initial / 8 MiB body and continuation read budgets for stored content and Kickstart source previews.
- Recover existing content from retained snapshots, preserving annotation anchors and commit associations. Incomplete or corrupt captures cannot be published as complete.
- Bound E2E memory and stream isolation fingerprints instead of loading entire existing data files.

## Issue

Fixes #332.

## Risk

**Tier C:** SQLite migration, capture fidelity, concurrent ingest, and full-content publication/redaction.

Migration V52 adds capture state and chunked full-text storage after unchanged shipped V50/V51. Existing rows remain explicitly incomplete until recovery succeeds; previews are never promoted to complete content by inference. `peasant harvest index --force` performs retained-first recovery with atomic annotation-preserving replacement when necessary. Publication reads both metadata and full content from the database in one snapshot; generated metadata sidecars are not required.

The branch is based on `develop` at `378f2f83`, including merged #334, #337, and #344. Current reviewed head: `b9eb645134feccdacb5b8ffcbdf4d7c5c5d98b0b`. #344's explicit load-versus-validation boundary remains intact.

The five existing harnesses retain complete accepted text, including Cursor framing examples, Claude multi-block system content, OpenCode compaction text, and Strike structured tool-output siblings. Upstream omissions prevent complete capture certification.

## Architecture

This C4 component view focuses on retained-content recovery and authoritative reads in the Peasant backend. Fresh ingestion uses the same capture/persistence boundary through the five existing harness adapters. Arrows show **data flow**, not execution order.

| Full-content loader | Component | Go | Verifies once and hydrates complete entries in one SQLite snapshot; `internal/store/content_reader.go`, `internal/transcript/loader.go`. Publication reuses the same on-connection helper from `internal/store/publication_metadata.go`. |
| Detail and export | Component | Go | Converts verified entries through the canonical transcript path; `internal/api/store_adapter.go`, `internal/export/sessions.go`. |
| Publication | Component | Go + redact | Redacts full entries before building multipart content and metadata; `internal/push/pipeline.go`. |
| Village | External software system | HTTPS API | Stores the explicitly published redacted transcript. |

### Relationships

| Retained artifacts | Capture and persistence | Saved records for backfill | File I/O |

title: feat: per-harness harvesting versions and freshness
body:
## Summary

Closes #223, #219, #220, #221, #252, #282.

Per-harness harvester versions: each harness (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi, Strike) carries its own adapter, indexer, and index-format version, and a change to one harness re-processes only that harness. The branch also repairs the integration of the Pi harness and database-authoritative content, which had left the suite red, and closes every failing test in the repository.

## What changed, by user-visible behavior

- **Only the changed harness re-indexes.** `HarvesterVersionRegistry` holds one version triple per harness; the harvest summary reports a per-harness map instead of one scalar; the version guard (`make check-harvester-versions`) proves every adapter or indexer change carries a version increase.
- **Previews show what is stored.** The session detail WebSocket, the kickstart preview pane, and the share wizard read the content the database holds, complete or not. Export and publication stay strict, with per-session refusals instead of run-wide failures.
- **Dry runs report and create nothing.** `peasant harvest --dry-run` on a fresh install forecasts the first harvest; `peasant push --dry-run` refuses when there is no database, with the repair named.
- **Large records.** Every harness reads, redacts, and indexes a transcript record up to 256 MiB whole. A record over the limit is omitted without being loaded, reported with a diagnostic, and marked in the stored entries by a placeholder that reads `only showing preview of tool output: full output is over the 256 MiB limit` at that tool output. Pi's private file, line, and line-count limits are retired. OpenCode reads rows without a size limit and refuses a managed projection by content, not by size.
- **Served detail stays under the contract cap.** Tool results, turn text, and tool arguments are bounded on the read path with a visible note under one document budget derived from one constant; the store keeps the full record; no session is refused for size.
- **A session with an omitted record can be published.** A capture incomplete only for that reason is publishable through one predicate shared by the writer, the readers, and both readiness queries; the request carries the partial flag and the omitted-record warning.
- **Freshness and read policy.** A stored session whose native file grew is re-read; a settled session touches no native input; a legacy row with a retained artifact is settled from that artifact; a failed re-read warns, keeps the last good data, and does not fail the run; an OpenCode source without event sequence numbers stores no cursor.
- **Database-first write path.** The database is the source of truth for a saved session and its transaction is the durability point. The retained transcript and metadata pair is backup input, written to a temporary directory and renamed into place transcript first and metadata last, with no file sync, no lock, and no journal. The per-harvest tree walks are removed, so an unchanged session reads nothing; a stale or torn pair is detected on the next read against the stored hash and repaired from the source. A one-time upgrade pass finishes any interrupted write an earlier build left behind and removes its lock files. `harvest index --all` rebuilds a lost or damaged database from the retained files. Stale peasant-written debug output is pruned while foreign files are kept.
- **Metadata schema.** One typed capture-format column with a CHECK constraint (migration 59); the metadata refresh rule is a declared set of refresh-free versions, so the next schema bump does not force a corpus re-harvest.

## Pins and migrations

- `github.com/peasant-labs/schema` v0.18.0 (unchanged from develop); `github.com/peasant-labs/redact` v0.1.5 (unchanged). No wire, schema-repo, or Village change.
- SQLite migrations 50 to 59; 59 renames `session_content_captures.capture_revision` to `capture_format` with a closed CHECK set and refuses an unmappable tag before it runs. Migrations 1 to 58 are untouched.

## Evidence

Every slice tip and every merged head was gated by one instrument: gofmt, go vet, ast-grep, go build, and the full `go test -race ./...` with package-line integrity checks (59 of 59 packages reported, no killed, timed-out, or panicking package, no data race), compared as failing-test-name sets against a pinned baseline. At the handoff CI run the suite showed 130 failing names, and the ingest package aborted on a nil-pointer panic that hid 52 more failing tests. At the landing head the full race suite exits 0 with zero failing names. The harvester version guard passed with `BASE=86ceb0b8 CANDIDATE=725cfa81`. CLI docs regenerate byte-identical apart from the generator date footer. The database-first write-path slice added its own proofs — a counting filesystem asserting zero syncs and zero reads of an unchanged pair, a write-ahead-log commit-frame counter, and source guards against syncs, locks, and extra hashes — and was reviewed by three axis reviewers (correctness, test quality, elegance) at zero blockers after its one blocker was fixed. Across the epic, review ended at zero blockers. CI run after the push: Tests run 34551614664 on 41b297ac passed (make check 21m43s, web build, web lockfiles).

## Residue

None. Every test that was failing at the handoff is green at the landing head. Follow-ups filed outside this PR: a first-class omitted-record field on the entry contract with a fairtrade warning component (contract ceremony); parser provenance on the wire (its own epic); a distinctive naming for peasant-written debug outputs; streaming the source read so an over-limit record is never loaded by the enclosing whole-file read; a redact-module note on the overflow contract; routing `peasant redact` through the shared atomic installer with a fault-injection proof; a database-first guard so the repair predicate does not re-list an unbindable OpenCode legacy row; and correcting the `harvest --data-dir` help so it does not imply peasant-sync moves with it. A small set of cosmetic minors remains.

## Component model

| Element | Type | Technology | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| peasant web | Container | Next.js | Renders the session detail it receives over the WebSocket. |
| peasant backend | Container | Go | Ingests, indexes, previews, exports, and publishes agent sessions. |
| ingest | Component | Go package internal/ingest | Discovers sessions, reads records up to the limit, omits over-limit records with a placeholder, and stamps per-harness versions. |
| store | Component | Go package internal/store | Owns the SQLite schema, captures, readiness, and the publishable-with-omissions rule. |
| transcript | Component | Go package internal/transcript | Turns stored entries into turns and applies the served bound. |
| push | Component | Go package internal/push | Preflights, redacts, and publishes a session. |
| peasant session store | Container | SQLite | Holds sessions, entries, captures, and version stamps. |
| agent session stores | Software System, external | JSONL files and SQLite databases | The harnesses' own recordings. |
| village | Software System, external | Go, Postgres | Receives published sessions. |

## Steady-state harvest performance (follow-up)

Once the store settles, a harvest no longer repeats work and no longer runs the comparison step on a single core.

- **Parallel comparison.** The DIFF stage classifies the discovery slice with a bounded worker pool and writes each result back at its discovery index, so the classification result and the discovery order are unchanged. On a warm-cache sandbox of the reference store the stage dropped from roughly 1.9 to 3.05 seconds to roughly 140 to 309 milliseconds, with identical counts (8,848 unchanged).
- **Settled refusals stay settled.** A session whose terminal capture refusal is recorded, whose indexer is current, and whose input proof is present no longer forces a native read or an index write. On the real store the second run went from 676 updated and 670 indexed to 7 updated and 1 indexed, and the run dropped from 5m25s to 2m58s.
- **Progress advances are monotonic.** The progress event carries a delta and the store owns the cumulative count, so a completion that lands out of order cannot move a bar backwards. The comparison order test is stable over 3,000 runs.
- **Docs and fixtures.** The ingest reference now describes DIFF as parallel. The refusal-churn fixtures reject an unknown key and a duplicate case name.

### Residual

79 extraction errors and 200 imported-but-not-indexed sessions remain on the real store. They are the documented permanent residual classes: strict-capture refusals, projection-shape mismatches, and incomplete retained input. The run reports them and does not retry them. No fail-open path was added.

### Gates

`go test ./...`, `go test -race ./internal/ingest ./internal/store`, `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, and `ast-grep` all pass on the merged tree. Two review rounds ran. The final round reported zero blocker, zero important, and zero minor findings from all three axes.

title: fix(title): derive the generated title from the first real user turn
body:
Closes #175. Related: #15, #45, #70 (cited, not duplicated), peasant-labs/schema#53.

## Problem
- `metrics.Engine.computeTitle` read the raw stored JSONL role and applied no injected reclassification at title time. It took the first depth-0 entry with stored role `user` and stopped there, so a session that starts with a slash command published `<command-name>/effort</command-name>` (or `<command-message>aura:research</command-message>`) as its title.
- `ingest.simpleTitle` fell back to the raw, unstripped first line on any pipeline error, so a malformed wrapper could leak a raw tag into the local display title.
- `web` left the view model untouched when no generated title existed, so the viewer derived a heading from the first prompt (a `<local-command-caveat>...` block could become the heading).

## Change
- `github.com/peasant-labs/redact` is pinned to the branch that strips command and local-command wrappers and adds `GenerateFromTurns` (peasant-labs/redact#14). Pinned to the final tag `v0.1.2` (vendor hash and `internal/moduleboundary/testdata/redaction.yaml` updated in the same change).
- `internal/metrics/engine.go`: `computeTitle` collects every depth-0 stored-user preview in order and calls `GenerateFromTurns`; empty and erroring turns are skipped (errors logged at warn); no title when nothing is usable. No pre-Generate skip predicate (a predicate would also drop `/skill <args>` turns whose args are the user's prose). `CurrentComputeVersion` 6 → 7 so a normal recompute picks the new titles up.
- `internal/ingest/title.go`: a pipeline error now skips the turn (returns empty) so `hints.title` advances to the next user line; the raw fallback is reachable only when the pipeline cannot be built.
- `internal/transcript/transcript.go`: the command-wrapper names come from redact's exported `Wrapper*` constants (one catalog); the role projection is unchanged.
- `web/src/components/session-detail/v2/SessionDetailV2.tsx`: always sets `session.title`; `Untitled session` when no generated title exists, so the composite never derives a heading from a raw first turn.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under Unreleased / Fixed.
