body: Closes #71. ## What Peasant now decides, once at import, who drove each recorded session, stores it, uses it on every discovery surface, and declares it on the wire. - **One typed rule** (`internal/sessionorigin`): `user | agent | unknown`. Ordered, first match wins: has a parent → agent; structured teammate identity (`agentName`/`teamName`) → agent; programmatic launch (`sdk-cli` + `sdk`) → agent; opening user record is a slash-command wrapper → user; opening record is a teammate handoff or a `Skill(/…)` bootstrap → agent; otherwise unknown. The adapter reads past harness-written scaffolding (caveat records) to the opening user record. Plain prose stays `unknown`, and `unknown` behaves exactly like `user` everywhere in Peasant. - **Storage:** migration **V46** adds `sessions.session_origin` (closed CHECK set, default `unknown`) and the evidence-cache columns. One versioned pass writes a verdict into every already-stored session at the next import; rows resolved without their transcript are not marked final and are re-checked later. - **Kickstart:** agent-driven roots are hidden from the picker; user and unknown roots stay. A visible parent shows `+ N child sessions` on its own line under the parent, one indent deeper, at every terminal width, counting its discovered children on the production path. - **Spawner re-parenting:** teammate roots are linked to the session that spawned them when the identity pairing is unique, so a parent push carries its whole tree. - **Lists vs links:** `GET /api/v1/sessions` applies selection scope + origin scope (sessions page, `/share` chooser). New `GET /api/v1/session-summaries?ids=` resolves links with no scope at all; `/share?sessions=` still opens a hidden session. Dashboard/trends totals keep selection scope only. - **Push:** `sessionOrigin` is always declared on the transcript payload; push never blocks on it. - **Contract:** re-pins `github.com/peasant-labs/schema` to `v0.1.2-rc1` (Local API 0.9.0, Types 0.13.0); nix `vendorHash` regenerated by the script. - **Fixtures:** every new or touched fixture uses required-name manifests; the real-store audit harness (`cmd/peasant-origin-audit`, build-tagged) and a two-run kickstart demonstration are committed; the contact-sheet gate now measures rendered content height and fails on overflow. ## Why Agent-heavy workspaces bury a person's own sessions under worker, reviewer, teammate, and subagent sessions. Real Claude Code data carries the evidence at import time; nothing downstream can recover it after the turns are folded. The producer that knows declares it; consumers stop guessing. Hiding is discovery scope only, never access control: a link always opens. ## Verification - `go test -race ./...` green (twice, non-cached); both build-tagged harnesses green; `gofmt`/`go vet` clean; title: fix(ingest): classify an injected OpenCode task result as a system entry
body:
## Summary
- An OpenCode background task that finishes injects its result back into the parent session as a user-role message. Its one text part carries the harness's own `synthetic` marker. Peasant ignored the marker, so the raw `<task ...><task_result>...</task_result></task>` XML stood in the transcript as a turn the user typed. The indexer now reads the marker and reclassifies that message to `role=system`, `entry_type=system`, on the same path `compaction`, `subtask`, and `agent` parts already use.
- The metadata flag alone decides this. There is no text-shape recognizer: a message a person wrote that quotes the same tag stays their own turn.
- **A message reclassifies only when EVERY one of its parts is synthetic.** OpenCode attaches a synthetic part to a message somebody really wrote whenever it annotates that message: a plan-mode reminder (`session/reminders.ts`), an attached file, an MCP resource, or an `@agent` mention (`session/prompt.ts` `resolvePart`, which emits synthetic parts under the person's own `messageID`). Keying on any single synthetic part would have stored their question as a system note. This is the line OpenCode itself draws at `session/prompt.ts:203`, where a user message is the person's own unless `parts.every(p => p.synthetic)`.
- No schema change. `RoleSystem` and `EntryTypeSystem` already exist. The child session stays a separate, linked session; no turn folding.

### Documented outcomes
- A synthetic part on an **assistant** message reclassifies that message too. The marker reclassifies whatever message holds it, exactly as a structural system part does. This is stated in the code comment and pinned by a fixture case.
- **Boundary, worth a follow-up.** The marker is read from the part data, so the fix covers every projection that carries stored part rows (the legacy SQLite projection and the JSON file store). The current-schema SQLite projection (`peasant.opencode.current-sqlite`, landed in #157) synthesizes a user message from the row's `text` field and pins no part-level marker, so a synthetic user row there would not reclassify. The upstream shape could not be confirmed from the available OpenCode source (v1.18.10, which predates that table), so this PR does not guess at it. If OpenCode persists the marker on the current schema, extending the normalizer is its own change.

## Issue
Fixes #253

## Risk
Tier B. One ingest classification path, no contract, no migration, no route. It changes what role a stored entry carries, so a re-index is what applies it to already-stored sessions.

## Verification
- `make check` - clean (full suite, race detector).
- `make build` - clean.
- `ast-grep scan --config sgconfig.yml .` - clean (a Go type gained a field).
- `go test -race ./internal/ingest -run 'TestOpenCodeToolTurnRendering|TestPipeline_ReindexReclassifiesAnInjectedOpenCodeTaskResult'` - ok.
- **Mutation proven red, both directions.** Dropping the `Synthetic` read fails the three reclassification cases (`message role = "user", want "system"`) and the integration test (`after re-indexing, the injected background-task result is stored as role="user" entry_type="text"`). Weakening the rule back to "any part synthetic" fails the mixed-message case with `message role = "system", want "user"`. Restoring the rule goes green.
- **Non-vacuity, both directions.** The `a-real-user-message-about-a-task-stays-a-user-turn` case stays green under the mutation, so the guard keys on the flag and not on the text. The integration test asserts the pre-state (`role=user`, `entry_type=text`) before re-indexing and fails the whole test if the first phase did not really store a user turn.

### Tests
- `internal/ingest/testdata/opencode_tool_turn_rendering.yaml` gains eight cases under the existing required-name manifest, no count guard. The four the issue asks for: a synthetic `completed` result, a synthetic `error` result, a real user message quoting `<task` without the flag, and a synthetic part on an assistant message. Four more pin the every-part rule against a wrong reading of it, each added because a review round proved the set could not yet tell the two apart: a real question carrying one synthetic annotation stays the person's own turn; a message whose two parts are both synthetic still reclassifies, which a one-part-only rule fails; a synthetic annotation ordered before the person's reply still leaves their turn, which a first-part-only rule fails; and a synthetic result beside a part type this indexer does not know still reclassifies, which counting unknown parts fails. The harness gains `want_message_role`, which every case now declares; the loader rejects a case that omits it.
- `internal/ingest/pipeline_opencode_synthetic_reindex_test.go` is the integration test over the real projection path: the real pipeline, the real OpenCode indexer, and the real store, run twice. The first run stores the session while the part carries no marker, which is the state every already-ingested session is in. The stored part is then replaced with the row OpenCode writes, and a `--reindex --force` run re-extracts from that storage. It asserts on entries read back from the store, so it proves the stale user row is replaced rather than shadowed, and it asserts the person's own message in the same session stays `role=user`.

## Visual review
Not applicable. No mounted UI change. The web viewer already renders a system entry as a system entry; this PR only changes which role an ingested entry carries. Peasant's web capture harness covers mounted surfaces, not a per-entry-role transcript fixture, so it has no existing capture of this path to re-shoot.

## Known gaps, not fixed here
- A depth-1 `tool` / `tool_use` part entry hardcodes `role=assistant` regardless of its parent's role (`openCodePartEntry`). This predates the change and this PR does not reach it: under the all-synthetic rule a message holding a tool part can never reclassify, because a tool part is never synthetic. Worth its own issue.
- A part type this indexer does not recognize is excluded from the every-part rule, so a message whose ONLY part is both unrecognized and synthetic keeps its stored role. No OpenCode version reaches this: every synthetic part it writes is a `text` or `file` part, both of which this indexer knows. It is recorded because the rule's goal is that harness-written content never stands as the person's own words, and a future part type carrying the marker would defeat that until the type is added to the known set.
- When a message mixes a person's part with a synthetic annotation, the annotation still folds to a turn of its own. That is the long-standing rendering of a second text part, not something this change decides. The fixture records the outcome honestly rather than asserting a rendering this PR does not deliver.

## Cross-repo impact
None required. Fairtrade's follow-up idea from the issue, a "background task finished" card for system entries of this shape, is a separate fairtrade change and is not needed for this fix: the entry already renders correctly as a system entry.

title: build(release): ship THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES + CI license guard
body: ## Ship THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES with the binary + a CI license guard Closes #363. peasant ships a **static binary** through Homebrew, deb, and rpm. `go build` strips every dependency's `LICENSE` out of the compiled artifact, so the permissive licenses of its Go modules (MIT / BSD / ISC / Apache-2.0 — all verified, zero copyleft) had no notice traveling with the binary. Those licenses require their copyright/permission notices to be reproduced on **binary** redistribution. This adds that file and keeps it honest in CI. ### What changed - **`scripts/gen-third-party-notices.sh`** — generates `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES` by enumerating the modules actually linked into `./cmd/peasant`, across all four release targets (linux/darwin × amd64/arm64) and **pinned to `CGO_ENABLED=0`** (the shipped build mode), then concatenating each module's **actual license text** from the Go module cache. - **`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`** — the generated, committed artifact: 64 license entries across the **58** third-party modules that actually ship (some modules carry multiple license files, e.g. the modernc stack's `LICENSE` + `LICENSE-GO`). - **`scripts/check-dep-licenses.sh`** — the copyleft guard: builds go-licenses once for the host, then runs `check` across all four targets, **failing closed on `unknown`** licenses and allowlisting only the vetted `modernc.org/mathutil` (BSD-3 the classifier can't match; its text still ships). - **`.goreleaser.yml`** — ships the file in the tar.gz archives (so the Homebrew cask carries it), the deb package, the rpm package (flagged `%license`), and the AUR `peasant-bin` PKGBUILD. - **`Makefile`** — `make third-party-notices` (regenerate) and `make third-party-notices-check` (the CI gate: freshness diff + copyleft guard). - **`.github/workflows/tests.yml`** — a `third-party-notices` job running the gate on every PR; the generator, guard, and notices file added to the `paths` filters. ### Why concatenate cache files instead of `go-licenses report` `go-licenses`' classifier cannot recognize the `modernc.org` SQLite stack's "The X Authors" BSD-3 variant, so `report` **silently drops** those modules — the exact modules whose BSD-3 terms require binary-form reproduction. Reading license **text** straight from the version-pinned module cache is deterministic and complete; a module with no license file becomes a hard error instead of a silent gap. `go-licenses` is kept for what it is good at — **classifying**, for the copyleft guard. ### Validation - **Build-mode correctness:** the module set is enumerated at `CGO_ENABLED=0` — exactly how the release binaries are built — so the file lists the 58 modules that ship (not the 7 cgo-only tree-sitter/go-pointer modules that a C-compiler host would pull in), and the gate no longer depends on the runner's toolchain. - **Coverage:** every shipped third-party module resolves to a license file (only the main module is excluded); the modernc/`mathutil` module `go-licenses report` drops is present. - **Deterministic:** repeated runs are byte-identical (`LC_ALL=C`, sorted enumeration + file discovery, pinned CGO, no timestamps). - **Gate is not vacuous:** fresh committed state → exit 0; a stale committed file → non-zero (mutation-tested). The hardened guard exits non-zero without the allowlist (proving `unknown` is enforced) and passes with it. - `goreleaser check` passes with the archive + nfpm + AUR additions. ### Scope Go modules only. The embedded web dashboard (`//go:embed all:web/out`) bundles npm packages whose notices ride along in the binary too; that is tracked as a follow-on in **#365** and called out in the file's header. ### Review Three-axis code review (correctness / design / compliance) on Claude Opus 4.8. Findings resolved in-branch: the CGO build-mode mismatch (BLOCKER), the guard failing open on `unknown` (IMPORTANT), the AUR PKGBUILD omission (IMPORTANT), the single-platform guard, `%license` flagging, the devShell requirement note, and the trap cleanup (MINORs). The Debian consolidated-`copyright` convention (info) is left as-is — we self-publish rather than target the Debian archive. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? title: fix(ingest): keep pair snapshots atomic and defer repair reads safely (#386)
body: Part of epic #388. Closes #386. ## Summary A forced rebuild (`peasant harvest --all`) could refuse sessions whose saved pair was actually intact: the index capture could pair an in-memory transcript with metadata bytes read separately at a later moment, so a concurrent pair write produced a checksum mismatch (`transcript checksum does not match committed metadata`). This PR makes the pair read atomic at every producer and narrows the selection-time repair read so it cannot skip a needed repair. - `captureArtifactForIndex`: when either half is in memory, both halves are read as one validated pair (`readArtifactPair`); an in-memory transcript always travels with metadata bytes from the same read or write. - Native-failure fallback: carries the exact validated `retained.MetadataJSON` beside the transcript it read, without claiming a committed artifact (no phantom mirror, no false publication). - `prepareReindexFallback`: reads both halves with `readArtifactPair` instead of a lone transcript read (the decoded publication projection would be lossy as metadata). - Deferred repair detection narrowed to proven-rewrite queues (forced run, native-refresh schema, newer clock that no stored fingerprint can overrule). Fingerprint-bearing newer-mtime rows keep the selection read, so a stale-index candidate with a damaged pair still gets its automatic repair. - Legacy OpenCode SQLite recovery behavior stays intact. ## Evidence Final gates at `231ce03c` (a comment-only commit on top of the code gate at `0002548b`): | Gate | Result | |---|---| | `go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30m ./internal/ingest/` | PASS (12m51s; no data races) | | `RACE=0 make check` | PASS (3m27s; 49 ok, 0 FAIL) | Behavioral red → green evidence: - Mixed-snapshot reproduction: pre-fix forced harvest refused (`Indexed 0`, checksum message) with the mid-run pair write; post-fix `Indexed 1` with entries from the original generation. - A genuinely torn pair (valid metadata + valid transcript from another generation) still refuses with the exact checksum error and changes nothing. - BLOCKER regression `queued-unchanged-source-damaged-pair-repairs`: RED with the pre-fix predicate, GREEN fixed; the stored-fingerprint selection-read guard is RED at 0 reads and GREEN at ≥1. - The concurrency overlap test is deterministic: a gated writer sits inside the production transcript-first/metadata-last window, and the production reader must attempt that window and refuse before the metadata write is released (no probabilistic counter). Review: wave 1 found one BLOCKER (fixed) and three MINORs; round 2 returned all ACCEPT with zero BLOCKER/IMPORTANT; the last comment-only MINOR was fixed and re-gated at the frozen head. ## Test plan - Fixture-driven pair-snapshot and deferred-repair corpora (`internal/ingest/testdata/*.yaml`) with required-NAME deletion protection. - YAML-backed production `Pipeline.Run` regressions for the mixed-snapshot and repair-preservation scenarios; torn-pair must-fail. - Selection-read measurement asserts exact behavior (0 reads for the deferred class, ≥1 for the fingerprint/readiness classes) with positive controls. --- Need help on this PR? title: fix(ingest): retain repair eligibility across interrupted pair installs
body:
## Summary
- Commit repair eligibility before replacing a previously settled saved transcript/metadata pair, through the existing serial database-write lane.
- Recover interrupted installs through ordinary harvest and index, including when native bytes and their clock have returned to the previous fingerprint.
- Preserve saved files and stored entries when the native source is unavailable, with the existing actionable repair diagnostic.

Fixes #393

## Risk and boundaries
Tier C: persistence and process-interruption recovery. No migration, wire change, new coordination mechanism, file sync/lock, or SQLite PRAGMA change.

The guarantee covers process termination while the operating system survives. It does not cover physical power loss, old unmarked corruption, or independent overlapping same-session writers. Index retains its existing metadata inventory and missing-row reconciliation; this change adds no repair inventory or unaffected-peer I/O above the ordinary command baseline.

## Verification
- `nix develop -c bash -c 'GOMAXPROCS=4 make check'` — passed, including the full Go race suite.
- `nix develop -c bash -c 'GOMAXPROCS=4 make build'` — passed.
- `nix develop -c bash -c 'ast-grep scan --config sgconfig.yml .'` — passed.
- Focused race tests for Store preparation, retained publication, unchanged write-path guards, existing mirror failures, and the mounted crash family — passed.
- Eight named YAML scenarios cover actual target renames followed by SIGKILL, ordinary harvest/index restart, unavailable source, intact-old/intact-new windows, SQL refusal before final renames, and baseline-relative peer I/O.
- Mutation: omitting only the shared preparation invocation made the primary mounted crash case fail after the confirmed real transcript rename and SIGKILL because `indexed_input_hash` remained non-NULL. Restoring the invocation restored the passing result.

## Visual and cross-repository impact
No layout or interactive UI changes; screenshots not applicable. No cross-repository contract/release dependency.

## Decisions awaiting your approval
- Restrict the recovery guarantee to process interruption while the OS survives.
- Preserve the existing index inventory rather than promise zero total traversal.
- Reuse the existing SQL input proof and writer ownership, without adding independent multiwriter coordination.

title: refactor(test): wait on signals and deadlines instead of fixed sleeps
body:
## What and why

Tests and two production paths waited with fixed durations or fixed-budget polls. That is an assumption about an idle machine: on a loaded or race-instrumented machine the waits either flake or burn their whole budget. This change makes every wait in the touched areas name its wake source or carry a deadline.

## What changed

- New leaf package `internal/testkit/testwait` (standard library only): a channel receive and a condition wait bounded by the test binary's deadline minus a grace period, with a one-minute fallback when no deadline exists (`go test -timeout=0`). Failures name the awaited state and the bound source.
- In-memory ingest tests wait on real signals: a new `entered` channel on the blocking indexer double, the existing downstream result channel, direct assertions after the `done` channel, a positive barrier before the write-lane negative check, and a synctest bubble where only a fake clock can prove the producer reached the arena wait.
- Test poll helpers in `internal/export`, `internal/store`, `internal/ingest`, `internal/githooks`, `cmd/peasant`, and `internal/tui/kickstart` now take their bound from the test deadline. The githooks subprocess retry keeps its pacing verbatim; only the attempt cap becomes the deadline.
- `peasant web start` (background) now carries a signal context. On Ctrl-C the readiness probe stops, the existing warning and URL, stop, and PID lines print, the browser is skipped, and the command exits with the cancellation error. `peasant open` stays budget-only.
- Ingest backpressure is stop-aware. The drain loop wakes on a published slot, finished workers, an acknowledged INDEX batch, or the context; the acknowledged-batch arm is required, or producers deadlock on a full arena. The arena wait wakes on a freed-space broadcast, a bounded 1 to 16 ms backoff, or the context. On cancellation, already-staged results keep the current per-session reporting, and the in-flight result is staged without an arena copy.
- The waiting policy is written down: a "Waiting in tests" section in `TESTING.md` (rule, decision tree, the three tools, negative-assertion and event-wake patterns, the keep list with reasons, the real-wait examples, fake-clock traps) plus the one-line rule in `AGENTS.md`.
- Two follow-on conversions: the store publication race budget now uses the shared bound rule, and the remaining fixed timers in the CLI and the export/store lock tests convert to signals and acquisition-order assertions.

## Evidence

- `make check RACE=1` on the merged head: PASS (two race-enabled passes with the exactly-once screen, the key gate, and the repo-wide ast-grep scan all green; the budget line reports its usual non-blocking warning).
- Targeted race runs and the two-pass test gate for every touched package: PASS on the final revision, with the screen rules satisfied.
- Three independent reviews over the full change (correctness, test quality, elegance and hygiene): no blockers, no importants. Eleven minor notes are tracked as follow-up tasks.
- The failure-mode checks recorded during the work: the cancel test fails on a `context.Background()` probe at about 4.9 s against its 2.5 s bound, and the full-arena pipeline test fails at its bound when the acknowledged-batch wake is removed.

## Boundaries

No public API, wire, route, response, or persisted-data change. The intentional real waits (cross-process locks, the subprocess retry, simulated latency, the response flush delay, the demo pacing) stay as they are and are named in the policy. No gate file, registry, or contract changed.

## Follow-ups (tracked separately)

- Making `peasant open`'s readiness wait cancellable.
- The review minors: doc wording for the stopped-result path, an exit-status assertion, the shared harvest bound note, the render-signal coverage note, bubble failure-mode documentation, two policy citation fixes, and two optional test additions.
- A load-sensitive nil-pointer crash in a third-party SQLite auth trampoline, observed once while the full gate ran under load; the affected test passes repeatedly standalone.

title: fix(e2e): eliminate harness flakiness on reused CI runners (rc1 blocker)
body: Closes #122. Fixes the e2e harness flaking on reused CI runners, which blocked rc1. Two layers: **isolation** so a prior run can't contaminate the next, and a **source-fix** so the village can't be orphaned in the first place. ## Root cause ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Run N-1: go test SIGKILL'd by cancel-in-progress"] -->|"t.Cleanup skipped"| B["leftovers survive on the reused VM"] B --> C["fixed bucket 'peasant-transcripts' keeps stale objects"] B --> D["orphaned village subprocess holds its port"] B --> E["leftover sandbox + peasant.db"] C --> F["Run N baseline reads S3 = 8, not 0"] E --> G["DIFF sees fixtures 'unchanged' -> pull ingested 0/6"] F --> X["FLAKY FAIL"] D --> X G --> X ``` The harness pruned leftover **sandboxes** at start (GUARD B1) but had no infra analog, the S3 bucket name was **fixed**, and `e2e.yml` only ran on push to `develop`/`main` — so the flake only surfaced post-merge. ## The fix ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph ISO["Isolation - 98f2faca"] A["per-run UNIQUE bucket: uniqueName transcripts"] C["GUARD B0: reap stopped + stale peasant-e2e-* containers"] E["age-based sandbox prune + UnixNano tokens"] end subgraph SRC["Source-fix orphaned village - Linux"] G["go test dies, any cause incl. SIGKILL"] -->|"kernel"| H["Pdeathsig SIGKILL + LockOSThread pin"] H --> I["village dies WITH the test, no orphan"] end A --> Z["deterministic baseline = 0 -> PASS"] C --> Z E --> Z I --> Z ``` **Isolation (`98f2faca`)** — per-run unique bucket threaded everywhere (the actual flake fix; documented in `docs/e2e.md`), GUARD-B0 stopped+stale-only container reaper, age-based sandbox prune, UnixNano tokens, `--include-active` pull ingest. Adds a path-filtered `pull_request:[develop]` trigger to `e2e.yml` so the full e2e gates PRs **pre-merge** — the gap that let this reach develop. **This PR self-validates via that new trigger.** **Source-fix orphaned village (`0309677c`, `80ab567f`, `e6e91e59`)** — a hard-crashed `go test` orphaned the village subprocess (`t.Cleanup` never runs on signal). Now killed at the source on Linux via build-tagged `SysProcAttr{Setpgid, Pdeathsig:SIGKILL}` + `runtime.LockOSThread()` (the mandatory companion — without it the runtime can retire the launching M and fire Pdeathsig early; golang/go#27505) + a `pid<=0`-guarded `killpg`-on-stop. Dead environ-scan scaffolding removed. macOS parity deferred (`2la0h`); Linux `Pdeathsig` is a forward-compatible subset of the portable inherited-pipe-EOF supervisor. ### Regression test (`village_procdeath_linux_test.go`) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant T as test participant P as re-exec'd parent participant G as sleep grandchild T->>P: re-exec via real setVillageProcDeath seam P->>G: spawn (Setpgid + Pdeathsig) P-->>T: report grandchild pid + /proc start-time T->>P: SIGKILL parent Note over G: kernel fires Pdeathsig on parent death T->>G: poll /proc until gone OR zombie OR start-time mismatch Note over T: GREEN: grandchild dies. RED (seam neutralized): survives -> timeout -> FAIL ``` The `/proc` start-time identity is anchored against `/proc/uptime` × CLK_TCK (proves token 19 genuinely is the start-time; excludes wrong stable fields), so the hardened test can't silently become always-green. ## Verification - `make check` ✓; cross-vet linux/darwin/windows (`-tags e2e`) ✓ - **10× consecutive** full-package `./internal/e2e/...` ✓ (the DoD) — reproduces the reused-host condition; the heavy `TestSkipGateE2E` / `TestPullRoundTripE2E` + the W4 regression all execute and pass - W4 RED/GREEN independently confirmed (neutralized seam -> FAIL; Pdeathsig -> PASS) - Driven through three standing-team review waves to **0 open findings** 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? title: feat(web)!: adopt the fairtrade design system across every surface
body: ## Summary The web dashboard's five surfaces — analytics, transcript viewer, code map, review, and the shell chrome — all render through `@peasant-labs/fairtrade` (^0.0.6), the shared design system, replacing the bespoke shadcn-era implementations. The user-facing outcome: every peasant surface is byte-faithful to the design system's canonical demo (typography, tokens, lowercase chrome, surface-staged backdrop), the deprecated `@peasant-labs/analytics` package is retired in favor of the design system's own `/analytics` entry, and the transcript viewer is the design system's `TranscriptViewer` composite rather than a hand-rolled sibling — making visual drift between apps structurally hard. The branch also carries the server-side work that live-scale validation surfaced: an N+1 annotation query batched into one, hub broadcast/snapshot scheduling fixes with panic-free connection teardown, and a stale-while-revalidate cache for project summaries. This is the peasant half of the cross-repo adoption (companion PR in **village**; the design-system releases 0.0.4–0.0.6 and transcript-browser 0.0.3 already landed on their `main`s). ## Testing - [x] Created tests - [x] Updated tests - [x] Tested via integration / simulation - [x] Tested manually (describe how) - [ ] No tests (reason): N/A ```bash # Go: full quality gate (fmt + vet + ast-grep + tests with -race) make check # Targeted: the hub teardown regression (fails under the old close-based teardown) go test -race ./internal/api/ -run TestSnapshotSendAfterUnregister -count=1 # Web: typecheck + unit/integration suite (685 tests) cd web && pnpm typecheck && pnpm vitest run # Full-app smoke: 12 surface checks on the real binary (builds, boots, captures) make build && CHROME_PATH=$(command -v google-chrome-stable) node web/scripts/visual/full-app-smoke.mjs ``` Manual verification ran against a real 2.9 GB store (7.6k sessions / 27 weeks): analytics first data render ~2s warm, chart axes legible at that scale, map task links open whole conversations positioned at the turn, `bin/peasant web start` exercised on all routes. ## Screenshots / Videos Theme-asserted captures from the full-app smoke on the real binary (regenerate via the smoke command above): `web/scripts/visual/smoke/{dark,light}/{analytics,transcript,map,dashboard,review-changes,review-change-detail}.png`. The committed `web/scripts/visual/baseline/` set is the regression baseline; attach the analytics + transcript pair to the PR when opening. ## Related Issues - peasant-labs/peasant#142 — the originating design-system adoption request this branch delivers. - peasant-labs/peasant#148 — durable analytics/statistics aggregates + sessions/projects pagination (the architecture follow-up this branch's caching quick-wins point at; deliberately not addressed here). ## Changes ### Analytics (`web/src/app/analytics/`, `web/src/lib/adapters/analytics.ts`) - The dashboard mounts the design system's `/analytics` surface; the standalone `@peasant-labs/analytics` package is retired. - A thin adapter maps quality-channel sessions onto the design-system-owned `AnalyticsSessionRecord`; sessions attribute to `'local user'` (an honest placeholder — the stream carries no contributor identity yet). ### Transcript viewer (`web/src/components/session-detail/v2/`) - `SessionDetailV2` is a thin host over the design system's `TranscriptViewer` composite: view model via `adaptTranscript` + `computeAnalytics`; host seams carry scoping, annotation popovers (`renderTurnActions`), per-turn wire panels (`renderTurnPanel`), origin-aware breadcrumbs, and real permalink anchors (`anchorHref`). - Map and palette task links deep-link `?turn=N` (typed `TurnParam`) — they position the viewer, never filter it. ### Map / review (`web/src/app/map/`, `web/src/app/review/`) - Canonical design-system composition, working zoom controls (consumes the upstream pointer-capture fix), lowercase chrome, origin breadcrumbs. - Project summaries render instantly on return visits via a module-level stale-while-revalidate cache (`web/src/lib/api/map.ts`). ### Shell (`web/src/app/layout.tsx`, `TopNavbar`, `SessionFilterBar`, `globals.css`) - The app stages on `--surface` exactly like the design-system demo; `--canvas` is the inset tone. Atkinson Hyperlegible self-hosted per the design system's contract. ### Server (`internal/api/`, `internal/store/`) - `GetSessionAnnotationsBulk`: quality snapshots fetch all session annotations in one query (was an N+1 of ~7.6k round trips). - The hub broadcast tick skips topics with zero subscribers; snapshot-on-subscribe runs off the hub goroutine; connection teardown never closes the write channel (a detached snapshot send can no longer panic the process — deterministic `-race` regression test included); post-teardown drops leave a debug trace. ### Visual harness (`web/scripts/visual/`) - Boot/mock/shoot/stitch/diff/probe/gate primitives + a 12-surface full-app smoke on the real binary; capture flows hard-assert theme and backdrop before taking pixels. ## Blast Radius - **Breaking for the web surface**: the shadcn `web/src/components/ui/*` kit is deleted; anything out-of-tree importing those paths breaks. All in-tree consumers migrated. - **Wire/links**: `?scope=task&scopeVal=N` task links are replaced by `?turn=N` at the link *sources* (map, palette). The scope-filter query params still parse — old bookmarked URLs keep working. - **Server**: hub changes are behavior-preserving for subscribers (same payloads); the teardown change removes a panic path. The bulk annotation query is additive; the per-session query remains. - **Dependencies**: fairtrade `^0.0.6` and transcript-browser `^0.0.3` from the registry; `web/` moves from npm/package-lock to pnpm (workspace + lockfile committed). - **Not affected**: TUI, CLI, ingest pipeline, publish/pull contract (no `pkg/schema` API changes; only shared test fixtures added). ## Checklist - [x] All relevant tests pass - [x] Quality gates pass (typecheck, lint, build) - [x] Documentation updated (if applicable) — `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` sibling-repo + harness sections, `web/docs/data-binding.md` - [x] No debug logs, commented-out code, or stray TODOs (the one `slog.Debug` is intentional, user-directed observability on the teardown drop path) - [x] Follows project coding standards (typed params/enums, ast-grep rules zero violations) ## Reviewer Notes ### Design decisions | Decision | Option A | Option B | Chosen | Rationale | |----------|----------|----------|--------|-----------| | Analytics consumption | Keep standalone `@peasant-labs/analytics` | Design system's `/analytics` per-surface entry | B | A sibling package that depends on the design system created a dependency cycle and per-app patch drift; a shared surface lives IN the design system | | Transcript viewer | Keep bespoke turn-list composer | Design system `TranscriptViewer` composite + host seams | B | Two apps hand-rolling the same viewer drifted (timeline, filters); the composite makes drift structurally hard and demo-fidelity the default | | Task deep-links | `?scope=task&scopeVal=N` (filtered view) | `?turn=N` (whole conversation, positioned) | B | Opening a pre-filtered single-request view was rejected at acceptance testing; positioning preserves context | | Hub snapshot delivery | Synchronous on the hub loop | Detached goroutine + never-close teardown | B | A slow cold snapshot (whole-store read) blocked every client and the tick; the teardown redesign removes the send-on-closed-channel panic the detachment would otherwise introduce | | Summaries latency | Backend materialization now | Frontend stale-while-revalidate cache now, materialization tracked (#148) | B | The cache is a contained quick-win; durable aggregates are a schema-level change deserving its own design pass | ### Problem space characterization - **Parallelism**: hub concurrency is the one genuinely parallel area — snapshot goroutines vs. the hub loop vs. teardown; resolved by a never-closed write channel and signal-based teardown (`done` + `closeOnce`). - **Scale**: validated at 7.6k sessions / 2.9 GB — the fixture-scale blindness that let "000" y-axis ticks ship is now covered by a live-scale story gate upstream and the real-binary smoke here. - **Has-a / Is-a**: peasant HAS thin adapters onto design-system surfaces; it IS NOT a design-system implementor — rendering logic belongs upstream (fairtrade / transcript-browser), and the adapter layer stays deliberately thin. ### Areas requiring attention - `web/src/lib/adapters/analytics.ts` stamps every session with the `'local user'` placeholder — when the quality stream gains real contributor identity, this is the single seam to replace. - The SWR summaries cache has no TTL by design (slow-moving per-ingest data, background refresh on every mount); if that assumption changes, add one. - The map's cold-store landing latency is mitigated, not solved — #148 is the real fix. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Refs #181. Kickstart consent wiring — the three kickstart acceptance criteria in
#181 — is deliberately **not** here and is tracked in #208, so this PR does not
close #181.

Adds opt-in, per-repository Git hooks that upload the current repository's recorded sessions to your village, without ever blocking ordinary Git work.

## What you get

```
peasant village hooks install --event post-commit [--event pre-push] [--dir <repo>] [--timeout <d>]
peasant village hooks status [--dir <repo>]
peasant village hooks uninstall [--event ...] [--dir <repo>]
```

Nothing is installed implicitly. You choose the repository and each event explicitly, and `--dir` defaults to the working directory.

The installed hook runs the ordinary command you could run yourself:

```sh
peasant --config '…' --data-dir '…' village push --non-interactive --quiet --timeout 5s --repository '/abs/repo'
```

`--quiet` and `--timeout` are part of the contract, not decoration:

- **`--quiet`** — a hook fires on every commit and every push, so the default multi-line summary would print into every ordinary Git command. Quiet still prints errors and one final result line, so a failure is never hidden.
- **`--timeout 5s`** — the village client's own timeout is **per request**, and one push issues several in sequence, so a village that accepts a connection and then stops answering (VPN, captive portal, stalled proxy) would hold Git up for minutes, once per commit. The budget caps the *whole* upload. Giving up is a warning, not a failure. `peasant village hooks install --timeout <d>` changes it; it is chosen at install time rather than by editing the file, because an edited hook is no longer one Peasant can rewrite or remove.

Under that budget the hook is **best effort but convergent**: anything the village accepted is recorded as published even if the budget expires while reading the answer, and a bounded run uploads its smallest sessions first, so each run turns its budget into progress instead of restarting the same oversized transcript forever.

## Safety properties

- **Git is never blocked.** A failed upload prints an actionable warning naming what failed, why, which repository and hook, what it means, and how to retry or uninstall, then exits 0. It does not claim nothing was published: an upload can succeed and the run still fail afterwards.
- **Existing hooks are never touched.** Only an absent slot is installed automatically. Anything already present — including a zero-byte file — is left byte-for-byte and mode-for-mode intact, and you get the exact snippet to paste in yourself. That snippet preserves the host hook's original exit status, so it cannot mask a pre-existing failure.
- **`core.hooksPath` is never written.** Ownership is decided against the repository's own Git directory first and its worktree second. A submodule's hooks live in `<parent>/.git/modules/<sub>/hooks` — outside its worktree, and still nobody else's — so a submodule is installable. A linked worktree (own Git dir `<main>/.git/worktrees/<name>`, hooks in `<main>/.git/hooks`) and a hooks path outside the repository are genuinely shared, are refused for automatic management, and fall back to manual instructions, so consent for one repository can never install behavior into a sibling.
- **Uninstall removes only Peasant-owned content**, verified immediately before removal.
- **`status` reports what is really true**: the command the hook actually runs, a repository that has been moved or renamed since install, a hook whose executable bit was cleared (Git silently skips those), and the visibility the upload will publish at — re-read every time, because `push.visibility` is one global, mutable setting.

## Repository scoping

`peasant village push` gains a `--repository <path>` flag: *only push sessions recorded in this Git repository*. It is useful on its own, and it is what makes the hook's promise true.

Scope resolves through the existing ingestion identity (`DeriveProjectIdentifiersWithGit`) using the same installation salt, so SSH and HTTPS remotes for one repository agree, and two remote-less repositories that merely share a folder name do not collide. It composes as a strict AND after configured selection, so it can only narrow what would otherwise be pushed, never widen it. A push that sends nothing says which of the three states it is in — nothing recorded here, recorded but excluded by another narrowing, recorded and already published — and never suggests dropping the scope.

Every place the command is shown to you — hook header, help text, generated docs, manual snippet, failure recovery, and install output — renders from the same builder as the command that actually executes. The one command meant to be typed by a person (the hook's "run it once by hand" line) drops the three flags that exist only because a hook runs it, and keeps the bound paths, so it reads the same store the hook does.

## Behavior changes outside the hook path

Three changes here are **not** confined to hooks, and are called out because they alter existing surfaces:

1. **The origin-remote walk now stops at the repository boundary for ALL ingestion**, not only for hook-scoped pushes. A repository nested inside another (a submodule, a clone inside a clone) previously inherited the outer repository's remote and therefore the outer repository's project identity; it now derives its own. **Sessions ingested before this change keep their old identity** and stay outside the inner repository's scope until they are re-ingested. This is visible **on the village** too: a nested remote-less repository whose sessions were already published keeps that old project hash there, while sessions ingested after this change arrive under the new one, so that project splits into two on the village until the old sessions are re-ingested and re-pushed. Re-ingesting is a per-session operation — see the exit-status and re-ingest notes below.
2. **`SilenceUsage` on `village push` changes every runtime error path of that command**, not only the hook path. Past argument validation, a failure now prints the actionable message alone instead of appending the whole flag listing. This also covers the flag VALUES validated inside `RunE` — a negative `--timeout`, an empty `--repository`, an unknown `--license` — which lose their usage block as well; only the misuse Cobra rejects before `RunE` (an unknown flag, a flag missing its value) still prints the flag listing.
3. **`--quiet` suppresses more than it used to, for EVERY caller of `village push`, not only for hooks.** A script already passing `--quiet` now also loses the resolved-scope line, the redaction report, the structured diagnostics below error level (a manifest that could not be fetched, quality metrics that could not be read), the schema-version preflight notice, and the multi-line half of the empty-state explanation. Errors and one final result line are still printed, and the empty-state summary line carries the diagnosis and the next command on its own.

4. **`peasant village push` exits `3` when it failed before making a single village request** — a missing or expired login, an unreadable config, a store that would not open, a repository scope that would not resolve. Other failures still exit `1`. The status exists because a generated hook sees nothing else: without it the hook reports an expired login as an upload that published part of its work. Scripts branching on a non-zero status are unaffected; scripts matching `1` exactly are not.

5. **The local-persistence budget is deliberately NOT derived from `--timeout`.** `--timeout` bounds the network; the SQLite write that records a transcript the village has already accepted must happen regardless, or the next commit re-sends it forever. That write gets its own 10s budget, so on a contended database the two compose **additively**: a bounded run can take up to its upload budget plus that persistence budget. It is generous compared with a row update and exists only so a database another process is holding cannot stall Git.

6. **The push empty-state, budget, and hook-warning messages were rewritten** (details above and below). Behavior with the new flags unset is otherwise equivalent to `develop`, apart from those message corrections and the exit status in point 4.

## Advice corrections in this round

Every remedy these surfaces print was driven into its own failure state and run verbatim. Eight did not work; three of them damaged a working setup.

| State | Old advice | New advice | Observed on re-run |
|---|---|---|---|
| A hook Git runs with another interpreter (the `#!/usr/bin/env python3` hook `pre-commit` installs) | paste the POSIX shell section into it | names the interpreter, withholds the section, and offers moving the file aside or calling the scoped command from that hook's own language | before: `SyntaxError: invalid decimal literal` + `error: failed to push some refs`; after: both remedies run clean and the push succeeds |
| A repository that was moved on disk, scoped push empty | `peasant ingest --force` | nothing — the recorded directory is gone, so re-deriving would lose the sessions | before: `1 session(s) are recorded for it` → `No sessions are recorded for scope`, unrecoverable, and the published-marker ledger went 0 → 3; after: not offered |
| Work recorded inside the repository under an identity the scope cannot reach | `peasant ingest --force`, in the detail lines only | `peasant ingest --force --session <id>` in the SUMMARY line, stating what the unscoped form does | after: re-derives that one session, scope 1 → 2, other projects' published markers intact |
| Moved repository, hook fires | `where`, `fix`, and `stop` all named the old path | refresh and stop rendered against the resolved worktree; the doomed upload is skipped | before: `cd: No such file or directory` and `is not inside a Git worktree`; after: both run clean |
| Failed upload | "drop `--quiet` and add `--verbose`" then printed the hook's own quiet, capped command | the by-hand command, which drops exactly those flags | before: byte-identical to the command that just failed; after: full summary and error table |
| Stale identity under `--quiet` | diagnosis only in the detail, which a hook never shows | diagnosis in the summary line | after: visible in the one line a hook prints |
| Global `core.hooksPath` install refusal | offered "run install from the repository that owns the hooks directory" | offered only when a repository really runs that file (proved by asking Git from it) | before: `is not inside a Git worktree`; after: absent there, present and runnable for a linked worktree |
| A generated section whose framing was broken | "delete the section, then run install" | states both endings: delete the file and install, or keep it and take the by-hand section install prints | before: install refused again and handed back the section — a loop; after: the outcome matches what the advice predicts |

Two further accuracy fixes: a budget that expired during local work no longer says the village did not answer (it names what actually ran out), and installing from the main worktree now discloses that linked worktrees run the same hook file.

Scope resolution no longer costs one Git subprocess per recorded directory. Git decides worktree membership by walking up for a repository boundary, which is pure `lstat`; that walk is now done directly and memoized across shared ancestors, with a fallback to Git for anything the filesystem cannot settle. Measured here: 150 recorded directories 166ms → 0.5ms, 600 directories 654ms → 2.0ms, paid before every upload on every commit.

## Tests

Fixture-driven, exercising the mounted commands and the real generated script:

- install/status/uninstall round trip; both events, handled independently
- refusal paths leaving foreign content untouched; composed-hook exit-status preservation
- repository topologies: plain, submodule, repository-local hooks path, linked worktree, outside hooks path
- an installed hook whose executable bit was cleared, which Git will not run
- exact argument vectors, including paths with spaces, quotes, and shell metacharacters
- two-repository scoping under both `mode=all` and selected multi-project config, including remote-less same-named repositories, asserting the intersection of configured selection and repository scope
- a village that accepts a publish and then stalls its response body: the transcript is uploaded exactly once across three commits
- a budget that expires before any upload, reported as the budget rather than as a SQLite error or an imaginary bad repository path
- a bounded run uploading smallest-first, and an unbounded run keeping its order
- the scoped empty state in all three of its worlds, and its one-line form under `--quiet`
- failing upload still exiting 0
- a hook whose shebang names another interpreter, and a compiled hook: no shell section offered, and what is offered instead
- a repository moved on disk: the hook's refresh and stop commands rendered against the resolved worktree, and the pinned upload not attempted
- the re-ingest remedy on both sides of its evidence gate, so the corpus proves it stays away as well as appears
- worktree membership answered for 150 recorded directories with zero Git subprocesses, a nested repository excluded, a missing directory excluded, and a symlinked component still asked of Git
- a budget spent on local work not blaming the village, and the exit status of a run that never reached it

All hook mutation happens in disposable temporary repositories with isolated `HOME`, `XDG_*`, and Git config, with assertions that the developer workspace, global config, and checkout hooks stay untouched.

Non-vacuity was verified by mutation: dropping the flag from the hook, ignoring it in push, skipping configured selection when it is set, collapsing remote-less identity, making the snippet always exit 0, reverting any displayed command to the unscoped form, deciding hook ownership on the worktree alone, binding the "mark pushed" write back to the upload budget, and disabling smallest-first ordering, making the interpreter check always accept a shell section, printing the re-ingest remedy without evidence, and removing the hook's check that its repository is still there each fail the suite.

`gofmt`, `go vet`, `-race` package tests, CLI docs freshness, and `make check` pass.

## Deliberately not here

- **Kickstart consent wiring** — the three kickstart acceptance criteria of #181. Tracked in #208.
- The authoritative publication receipt/visibility contract work, tracked in peasant-labs/schema#48.



---

## Also in this PR: redaction is honest about what it does

Shipping an automatic upload path forced two things to be true that were not.

### Maximum redaction refuses instead of silently weakening

Maximum was the only level that transformed transcript **content**, and it was broken: with no
origin remote, entropy detection rewrote the stored host slug, so push looked for a directory that
was never written and that repository could **never publish again** — permanently, on 15-37% of
untracked repositories.

It now **hard-fails** with an actionable error naming the setting and the value to use, at every
door that could reach it (push, the three ingest paths, `peasant redact --level`, and both web
endpoints). The kickstart wizard no longer offers it. Downgrading silently was considered and
rejected: it would have moved those users from anonymized published code to raw published code,
in a release whose own message told them nothing was wrong.

Closes #210 — the underlying slug corruption is repaired here rather than deferred. The directory,
the database row, and the metadata file now record the same location; the slug stays real on disk so
paths resolve and is still redacted on the wire by the existing outbound safety net.

### The product stopped claiming redaction it does not perform

Transcript **content is published as recorded** — that is the intended behaviour for now, recorded
with its rationale in #211, because content redaction at the supported level replaces whole fenced
code blocks and would destroy the artifact this tool exists to share.

Several surfaces claimed otherwise. The push consent screen said *"No raw data will leave your
machine"*; `docs/NETWORK.md` — the user-facing privacy reference — promised data leaves only on
explicit action, in the branch introducing the first automatic upload path, and did not mention
hooks at all. Both are corrected, along with the developer document they would have been
re-derived from.

Redaction language is now best-effort throughout: it matches **known patterns** and cannot promise
every instance was found. Secrets keep a stronger statement, because the village runs its own
server-side scan and rejects a publish carrying them independently of client-side matching.

## Verification

- `make check` green, `nix build .#peasant` green, `go test -race` green
- The joined end-to-end chain — real git → generated hook → real peasant → real village — passes
  **10 of 10 consecutive runs**, against a **5-of-8** control on the base commit. The flake was the
  redaction defect above; removing it from the path made the oracle deterministic.
- Every guard is mutation-proven: each was reverted and observed to fail. Several were rewritten
  after mutation showed they passed while proving nothing.

## Deferred, with issues

#212 (the oracle observes nothing of the published payload), #213-#219. None blocks this change;
each is recorded with what was verified and why it was deferred.

title: fix(redact): reduce false positives + grouped redaction sidebar UI
body:
## Summary

- **Fix AWS_SECRET_KEY false positives** — added `FilterFn` on `Rule` struct with context-only `awsSecretKeyFilter`: requires AWS-specific keywords (`aws_secret`, `secret_access_key`, `access_key`, `credential`, `amazon`) or AKIA prefix within 200 chars. Bare "secret"/"password" removed (too common in coding transcripts). File paths, git SHAs, base64 strings no longer flagged.
- **Fix CREDIT_CARD false positives** — added `creditCardFilter` rejecting dash-separated UUID fragments (8-4-4 pattern). Real credit cards use spaces or no separator.
- **Fix `${2}` displaying in UI** — regex back-references (capture group placeholders that preserve trailing boundary characters during actual redaction) were shown literally in the web UI. `displayReplacement()` now strips them for display.
- **Unify RedactText pipeline** — refactored `RedactText()` step 2 from sequential `applyRule()` to `Detect()` → filter → `Redact()`, so both the sync handler (web UI) and actual redaction share filtering logic.
- **161-case YAML fixture corpus** — covering all 50 redaction rules, loaded via `//go:embed`, table-driven tests.
- **Sidebar navigation UI** — left sidebar with Category > Rule tree (counts + click-to-filter), main content shows filtered items. Fixed 50-item cap per rule group. Server-side `GroupedRedactionResponse`.

Closes #32

## Architecture

```
Detect(input) → for each Rule:
  regex match → FilterFn != nil?
    YES → FilterFn(matched, input, offset) → true=keep, false=reject
    NO  → keep all
  → sorted []Match

awsSecretKeyFilter:
  1. Pre-filter: reject sequential strings, UUIDs
  2. Scan 200-char window for AWS keywords or AKIA prefix
  3. Context found → keep | No context → reject

Regex back-references (${2}):
  Pattern: (base64{40})(boundary_char)  →  Replacement: <AWS_SECRET_KEY>${2}
  ${2} re-inserts the trailing " or \n so surrounding text isn't corrupted.
  Bug: sync handler displayed raw "${2}" instead of expanding it.
  Fix: displayReplacement() strips back-refs for display only.

Sidebar UI:
  ┌──────────────┬──────────────────────┐
  │ Filter by    │ Summary cards        │
  │ ▼ Credentials│ 🔑 3612  👤 123     │
  │   AWS_SECRET │ Showing: AWS_SECRET  │
  │   ANTHROPIC  │ L222: nttea/code...  │
  │ ▶ PII        │ L482: vidpham/be...  │
  │ ▶ Paths      │ ... (50 of 3,400)   │
  └──────────────┴──────────────────────┘
```

| Large (135,767) | 135,767 | 0 | 0 | Fixed |

```
  └

[3] assistant  13:07:19  depth=0  ◀ center

[4] text  --:--:--  depth=1  parent=3
  Let me use Grep instead:
```

Full `--help`, `--json`, sort/filter outputs are embedded in #37.

---

## Key design decisions

These resolved during Plan UAT (`unified-schema-a3jex`) and Implementation UAT (`unified-schema-elhxe`) — the proposal evolved significantly from its first draft.

### 1. Entry_index addressing, NOT folded ordinals

**Decision:** `--turn N` addresses `session_entries.entry_index` directly. No "ordinal" concept.

**Why:** The original proposal had dense ordinals (post-`EntriesToTurns()` position) translated to sparse entry_index for DB queries. The user pushed back: entry_index is already sequential in the DB, and annotations reference entry_index, so introducing a separate ordinal layer adds confusion without benefit.

**Implementation:** Single SQL range query — `SELECT * FROM session_entries WHERE session_id=? AND entry_index BETWEEN ? AND ? ORDER BY entry_index`. No `EntriesToTurns()` invocation in the context command path.

### 2. `-C K` = raw entry range, not folded turns

**Decision:** `-C 1` returns entries at indices `[N-1, N+1]` literally — including depth=1 tool children if they fall in the range.

**Why:** Matches `grep -C` semantics (lines in the file, not "logical" units). The user wanted raw, unfolded entries with each `tool_use`/`tool_result` shown as its own row.

**Implementation:** Range query is unconditional on `depth`. Renderer indents depth=1 entries under their depth=0 parent for visual hierarchy but doesn't merge them.

### 3. Project matching: `canonical_remote` first, `canonical_cwd` basename fallback

**Decision:** `--project peasant` matches `canonical_remote LIKE '%peasant%'` first; if no match, falls back to `basename(canonical_cwd) == 'peasant'`.

**Why:** Reviewer A flagged the original "canonical_cwd basename" approach as collision-prone across machines. The DB already has a normalized git remote URL (`github.com/owner/repo`) per session; using it makes filtering portable.

**Implementation:** New `SessionListFilter.ProjectName` field; CLI translates `--project` to this. Listing always exposes `canonical_remote` (added to `SessionRow` and `sqlAllSessions` JOIN).

### 4. Single JSON object for context, JSON array for list

**Decision:** `peasant sessions context --json` emits `{sessionId, centerIndex, contextRadius, maxEntryIndex, entries: [...]}`. `peasant sessions list --json` emits `[{id, date, project, turns, tokens, preview}, ...]`.

**Why:** Context has session-level metadata (the center, the radius, the boundary) that wouldn't fit JSONL. List is a flat collection where an array is the natural shape and pipes well to `jq`.

### 5. Bare `peasant sessions` shows help + listing

**Decision:** Override cobra's default RunE to print help text, then run a default listing below it.

**Why:** Discoverability — new users see available subcommands AND recent data without typing anything else. Cobra's default behavior (print help and exit) wastes the user's first interaction.

### 6. Full IDs and full project names — no truncation

**Decision:** ID column is dynamically sized to fit the longest session ID. Project column is dynamically sized to fit the longest project name.

**Why:** Truncated IDs (`agent-a3...`) are unusable for copy-paste into `--session`. Truncated project names hide which repo a session came from. Discovered during Implementation UAT — the original implementation truncated both.

### 7. Relativized file paths in context output

**Decision:** When rendering an entry's content_preview, strip the session's `canonical_cwd` prefix from any matching path-like strings.

**Why:** Tool output (e.g., `find` results) frequently contains absolute paths like `/home/minttea/dev/agent-data-leverage/...` that bloat the display. Surfaced during Implementation UAT catch-all.

### 8. Deferred to follow-up (epic `unified-schema-8iyw5`)

- `--show-full-content` flag — re-index source transcript for complete (untruncated) content
- `--format-tool-calls={compact,quiet}` — verbose is MVP default and only mode
- Annotation filtering — `--annotated`, `--annotation-kind`, `--annotation-status`
- `--columns` — custom column selection
- N+1 query optimization for FirstUserMessage previews (currently one query per row)

## Summary
Fixes #63. After #59 added branch-level `selection` to `peasant village push`, the **interactive** path diverged from `--dry-run`/the pipeline: the wizard listed all ~7,000 sessions (ignoring `selection`), `--yes` didn't skip the wizard, and there was no fully non-interactive push path. This PR makes the wizard selection-aware, adds a canonical `--non-interactive` flag (with `--yes` as a backward-compatible alias), and adds output-verbosity control.

## What changed
- **Selection-aware wizard (R1/R6).** New shared `push.QueryPushCandidates(ctx, store, PushCandidateQuery{Force, SourceProvider, Method})` is the single base-query path; both `pipeline.getTargetSessions` and the wizard route through it (closing a previously-silent `by-source` divergence). The wizard list is filtered by the same `push.ApplySelection` the pipeline uses, so **wizard view == `--dry-run` == actual upload** for a given selection (asserted across all 5 query modes).
- **Withheld sessions shown, locked.** Multi-project branch-conflict (AND-strict) sessions appear in the TUI flagged `withheld: branch conflict` and are **non-selectable** (`PushWizardSession.Locked`; `PushAction` stays binary).
- **`--non-interactive` (canonical) + `--yes` (alias).** Both skip the session wizard **and** the public-consent prompt and push exactly the configured selection — for scripts/CI. `--yes` is preserved as a true alias (`--help` labels it `(alias for --non-interactive)`).
- **Output verbosity (`--quiet` / `--verbose`).** Typed `outputLevel` enum. Default = concise summary; `--verbose` (pre-existing) = per-session detail; `--quiet` = errors + final result line only. `--quiet --verbose` together is an actionable error. `--json` is unaffected.
- **Empty-selection no-op.** A configured selection that matches zero pushable sessions exits 0 with a clear note (gated on the base candidate count via new `PushResult.BaseCandidateCount`, so it doesn't misfire for nothing-ingested / all-already-pushed).
- **Output streams.** The public-push redaction report stays on **stderr**; the push **Summary** stays on **stdout** (record of what was published).

Real `push` command against a real seeded SQLite store (SUT not mocked): `WizardEqualsDryRunEqualsPipeline` (5 modes), `BuildPushWizardSessions_SelectionAware`, `NonInteractiveAlias_SkipsInteractive`, `PublicConsent_ReportOnStderr_NonInteractive`, `Quiet_SuppressesReport`, `EmptySelection`/`NothingIngested`/`AllAlreadyPushed` note gating, `ResolveOutputLevel`, plus wizard units. `make check` green (fmt, vet, ast-grep 0 violations, `go test -race ./...`). title: feat(ingest): add Cursor transcript ingestion
body:
**Summary**

Implements full Cursor transcript support in the peasant harvest pipeline. Cursor stores agent sessions as JSONL at ~/.cursor/projects/{workspace}/agent-transcripts/{sessionId}/{sessionId}.jsonl, with subagents at .../{parentId}/subagents/{sessionId}.jsonl.

**What's new**

- CursorAdapter (internal/ingest/cursor.go): Discovers root + subagent sessions by walking ~/.cursor/projects, decodes Cursor's workspace slug (dashes encode path separators, underscores, and spaces — all three variants are tried per segment), extracts metadata (model, token counts, turn count, timestamps, subagent refs), and enriches project identity via git with walk-up fallback.
- CursorIndexer (internal/ingest/cursor_indexer.go): Parses Cursor JSONL into SessionEntry slices. Handles both PascalCase (ReadFile) and snake_case (read_file) tool names via classifyCursorToolKind. Strips <user_query> and <timestamp> wrapper tags from user messages so content previews show the actual query text.
- Default source path: ~/.cursor/projects (enabled by default in BaseConfig()).
- Pipeline wiring: HarnessCursor is registered in the adapter factory, indexer map, applySourceOverride, buildSourceConfigs, kickstart wizard ingest runner, and the --source-provider CLI flag.

**Changes to existing code**

- internal/ingest/utils.go (new file): Extracted shared helpers out of claude_indexer.go — decodeProjectSlug, parseIndexTimestamp, isSystemInjectedContent, parseSkillInvocation, extractCommandName/Args, truncateString. Pure move with no behavior change to Claude indexing.
- internal/ingest/claude_slug.go: DecodeClaudeSlug now delegates to the shared decodeProjectSlug core. Behavior is identical; the refactor lets Cursor's slug decoder share the same greedy segment-matching logic via its own cursorSegmentVariants callback.
- pkg/schema/types.go: HarnessCursor added to AllHarnesses (previously excluded with a "not yet implemented" comment). This widens the kickstart wizard provider list and any other callers that enumerate AllHarnesses — provider count assertions in ftue/page_test.go were updated from the hardcoded 4 to len(defaults.AllHarnesses).
- internal/store/schema_v23.go: Added 'cursor' to the sessions_v2 model_harness CHECK constraint so fresh databases accept cursor sessions without needing the repair path.
- internal/tui/ftue/wizard.go: The Claude Code retention page is now skipped when zero Claude Code transcripts are discovered, rather than always shown. Prevents showing Claude-specific configuration to users who only have Cursor or other transcripts.

**Database compatibility (blast radius)**

Existing databases have CHECK (model_harness IN ('claude','opencode','codex','gemini')) on sessions and daily_summary_harness — 'cursor' is absent. Without repair, InsertSessions would fail with a constraint violation for any Cursor session.

schema_cursor_repair.go (applyCursorHarnessSchemaRepair) runs at store.Open() time, gated on PRAGMA user_version < 33. V33 formally adds 'cursor' to both constraints via migration, so the repair is a guaranteed noop for databases already at V33+. The repair uses the standard temp-table + INSERT INTO ... SELECT + rename pattern inside a transaction with FK constraints temporarily disabled. All existing rows are preserved.

**Test coverage**

- cursor_test.go: Discover (nested layout + subagents, path resolution, CWD decoding, title extraction); ExtractMetadata (model, tokens, turn count, subagent refs, project name); CursorIndexer (full-depth blocks, malformed line skip, part type, <user_query> stripping at depth 0 and 1, tool kind classification for both PascalCase and snake_case names).
- cursor_slug_test.go: decodeCursorSlug (full/partial/no match, underscore and space variants, precedence of literal dash over underscore), cursorSegmentVariants, decodeCursorWorkspace.
- cursor_harness_repair_test.go: V32-downgrade path (open triggers V33 migration which includes the repair), direct V24 path (open with WithSkipMigrations exercises applyCursorHarnessSchemaRepair directly).

body:
## Summary

Adds the complete binary-release and packaging pipeline for peasant: a maintainer-gated `release(vX.Y.Z[-rcN])` PR ceremony that auto-tags and triggers a goreleaser build of statically-linked binaries for linux/{amd64,arm64} + darwin/{amd64,arm64}, with deb/rpm packages, checksums, and CI-validated (publish-gated) AUR/Homebrew/Nix packaging. This is the release/packaging blocker for taking the repo public (#82 scope guard: no history work), delivering #90 and the rpm/WSL freebies of #91. Originating REQUEST: Beads `unified-schema-gn1y3`; URD: `unified-schema-ascmu`; ratified plan: PROPOSAL-3 `unified-schema-eq3ei`.

## Architecture

### Release Signal Chain: PR Title to Published Artifacts

```
Maintainer opens PR to develop:  "release(v0.1.0-rc1): first release candidate"
  │
  ▼
release-pr.yml · validate job (PR open/edit)                ←── NEW (this MR)
  │  release-guard parse-title  ──→ grammar gate (exit code)
  │  release-guard check-maintainer --user $PR_AUTHOR ──→ admin/maintain gate
  │
  │  ≥1 APPROVED review from admin/maintain + merge
  ▼
release-pr.yml · tag job (closed && merged)                 ←── NEW (this MR)
  │  re-parse title → $GITHUB_OUTPUT {version, kind}
  │  re-check approver via the SAME check-maintainer predicate
  │  mint App token (Contents:write)   ←── GITHUB_TOKEN tags can't trigger workflows
  │  refuse existing tag (local AND remote) → git tag -a $VERSION $MERGE_SHA → push
  ▼
release.yml · guard job (on: push: tags: 'v*')              ←── NEW (this MR)
  │  parse-tag (defense-in-depth; pkg/schema/v* rejected)
  │  if kind == final:  check-final ──→ green same-version rc AND
  │                                     git merge-base --is-ancestor rc final
  ▼
release.yml · release job (ONE linux runner, CGO_ENABLED=0)
  │  make web || make web-stub      ←── embed satisfied either way
  │  goreleaser release --clean
  │     ├── archives  peasant_{ver}_{os}_{arch}.tar.gz   ←── FROZEN naming contract
  │     ├── checksums.txt (SHA-256)
  │     ├── nfpm → .deb + .rpm  (empty Depends; static binary)
  │     ├── aurs → peasant-bin PKGBUILD        (skip_upload: true until flip)
  │     └── homebrew_casks → tap cask          (skip_upload: true until flip)
  ▼
GitHub Release (prerelease auto for rc)
  │
  ├── smoke job: native amd64 + arm64 runners download released tarballs
  │     ldd → "not a dynamic executable" · peasant version == tag
  │
  └── rc tags only: workflow_call → release-validate.yml   ←── NEW (this MR)
        deb 2×2 (ubuntu 22.04/24.04 × amd64/arm64) · rpm (fedora, leap)
        makepkg (archlinux, x86_64) · brew style · macos-15 cask install
        nix build .#peasant
```

### Component Ownership: Policy in Go, Orchestration in YAML

```
internal/release (pure, no I/O)                             ←── NEW (this MR)
  ├── Version    newtype  ^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\d+)?$  (NewVersion constructor)
  ├── ReleaseKind enum    {invalid, rc, final}
  ├── ParseReleaseTitle / ParseTag      ←── grammar defined ONCE
  ├── IsMaintainer(CollaboratorPermission)  ←── {admin, maintain} defined ONCE
  └── CheckFinal(final, []RCStatus)     ←── final-requires-proven-rc, pure decision
        ▲
        │  decisions (pure data in, error out)
        │
cmd/release-guard (thin CLI adapter)                        ←── NEW (this MR)
  ├── parse-title / parse-tag  ── emit version=…\nkind=… → stdout + $GITHUB_OUTPUT
  ├── check-maintainer ── gh api collaborators/<user>/permission
  └── check-final      ── git tag --list · git rev-list · git merge-base --is-ancestor
        ▲                  gh run list --workflow release.yml (SHA-matched, green?)
        │  6 call sites, exit code = the gate
        │
.github/workflows/{release-pr,release,release-validate}.yml ←── NEW (this MR)
  └── decide WHEN to call + wire tokens/secrets; never WHETHER to proceed
```

### CGO Build-Tag Seam: One Binary Family, Fail-Closed Redaction

```
NewRedactor(level)
  │
  ├── level != Maximum ──────────────→ regex/entropy pipeline (unchanged, pure Go)
  │
  └── level == Maximum
        │
        ├── //go:build cgo   (dev shell, make build)
        │     maximum_cgo.go:    MaximumAvailable = true
        │     newMaximumAnonymizer() → Fallback{TreeSitter → Regex}   (unchanged)
        │
        └── //go:build !cgo  (release binaries, CGO_ENABLED=0)        ←── NEW (this MR)
              maximum_nocgo.go:  MaximumAvailable = false
              NewRedactor returns ACTIONABLE ERROR (flag AND config path):
                "maximum … requires code-aware (tree-sitter) anonymization …
                 Falling back to weaker redaction is refused … use standard,
                 or a cgo-enabled build"
              factory panics if guard is ever bypassed (defense-in-depth)

CI gates: CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...                      ←── regression tripwire
          CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./pkg/redact/ ./internal/e2e/   (error-path asserts,
          PASS-not-skip; full AST differential still gated under CGO=1 make check)
```

### Artifact Fan-Out: One Frozen Naming Contract, Many Consumers

```
.goreleaser.yml  (single source of the name template)
  │
  │   peasant_{{.Version}}_{{.Os}}_{{.Arch}}.tar.gz + checksums.txt
  │
  ├──→ release.yml smoke job          (gh release download --pattern …linux_$ARCH…)
  ├──→ aurs peasant-bin               (source_x86_64/source_aarch64 URLs + sha256)
  ├──→ homebrew_casks                 (per-arch url stanzas)
  ├──→ docs/install/*.md              (manual download instructions)
  └──→ [future: curl-install script]

flake.nix package (independent build path, same ldflags version target)
  └──→ nix build .#peasant  → static, shortRev-stamped     ←── REWRITTEN (this MR)
```

## Testing
- [x] Created tests
- [x] Updated tests
- [x] Tested via integration / simulation
- [x] Tested manually (describe how)
- [ ] No tests (reason): N/A

### How to run

```bash
# Full quality gate (fmt + vet + ast-grep + race tests, both Go modules)
make check

# The new CGO=0 leg (mirrors the tests.yml cgo0 job; no -race: race needs cgo)
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./... && CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./pkg/redact/ ./internal/e2e/

# Release-policy table tests (grammar must-fail set, CheckFinal all 7 branches, IsMaintainer)
go test -race ./internal/release/ -v

# Module-zip / go-install proxy gate (proves the committed web/out placeholder)
git archive HEAD --prefix=zip/ | (cd "$(mktemp -d)" && tar x && cd zip && CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./cmd/peasant)

# Nix package (static, shortRev-stamped, emits the hard error at maximum)
nix build .#peasant && ldd result/bin/peasant; ./result/bin/peasant version

# Goreleaser config + workflows lint
nix develop -c goreleaser check && nix develop -c actionlint
```

Manual verification performed: `CGO_ENABLED=0` binary → `ldd` "not a dynamic executable", `peasant redact --all --level maximum` → actionable refusal; `release-guard` demos (valid rc title, malformed title, `pkg/schema/v9.9.9` all behave per spec); real `goreleaser release --snapshot` run inspected (`dist/` artifact names match every consumer glob). Container/macOS install jobs and the App-token tag→trigger chain are only exercisable in live CI — the post-merge `v0.1.0-rc1` run is their planned proof.

## Screenshots / Videos

N/A — CLI/CI-only change; representative terminal outputs are inlined under Testing (static-link check, hard-error refusal, release-guard gate demos).

## Related Issues

- #90 — release/packaging blocker (implements; research commented there)
- #91 — non-blocking distros (rpm artifacts + WSL docs land here as freebies)
- #82 — public-flip parent (release/packaging scope ONLY; no history work)
- Beads: REQUEST `unified-schema-gn1y3` · URD `unified-schema-ascmu` · PROPOSAL-3 `unified-schema-eq3ei` · IMPL_PLAN `unified-schema-x931f` (slices S0–S7) · Plan UAT `unified-schema-igdn2` · Impl UAT `unified-schema-1rt6e` · FOLLOWUP `unified-schema-divhp`

## Changes

**Release policy & workflows**
- `internal/release/` — typed `Version`/`ReleaseKind`/`CollaboratorPermission`, single-source title/tag grammar, pure `CheckFinal` (green same-version rc + ancestor), single-source `IsMaintainer`; table-driven tests incl. the must-fail grammar set
- `cmd/release-guard/` — thin CLI (`parse-title`, `parse-tag`, `check-maintainer`, `check-final`), `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` emit contract, fail-closed git/gh query assembly
- `.github/workflows/release-pr.yml` — dual-trigger gate + App-token annotated tagging, tag-collision refusal (local + remote)
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — guard → goreleaser → native-arch smoke; rc-only packaging fan-out
- `.github/workflows/release-validate.yml` — snapshot → deb/rpm/makepkg/brew/nix/macos install matrix
- `.goreleaser.yml` — 4 targets, frozen archive naming, checksums, nfpm `[deb, rpm]` (direct empty-Depends CI assert), `aurs` + `homebrew_casks` with `skip_upload: true`
- `.github/actionlint.yaml` — Blacksmith runner labels (repo-wide actionlint now clean)

**CGO elimination**
- `pkg/redact/` — `//go:build cgo` on tree-sitter (+test), `maximum_{cgo,nocgo}.go` seam with exported `MaximumAvailable`, hard-error on both flag and config paths, fail-loud `!cgo` factory; CGO=0 leg + config-path integration test in `internal/e2e`
- `.github/workflows/tests.yml` — `cgo0` job (CGO=0 build + tests) + module-zip proxy gate

**Packaging & fixes**
- `flake.nix` — package rewritten: pname `peasant`, `env.CGO_ENABLED=0`, real vendorHash, shortRev+ldflags version, web-stub `postPatch`, no `-race` checkPhase (cgo), honest non-SPDX `meta.license` (`free = false`); devshell + goreleaser/actionlint
- `web/out/index.html` placeholder + `.gitignore` ordering fix (both files) + `ReadBuildInfo` version fallback — un-breaks `go install`
- `internal/browser/` — `$BROWSER → xdg-open → wslview` chain, dedupes `cmd_web.go`/`auth/login.go`/ftue call sites, error surfaced at all three (fixes silent WSL failure)
- `Makefile` — `web-stub` target consolidating 3 inline stub copies
- `LICENSE` — open-webui-style placeholder (`LicenseRef-Peasant-Placeholder`); final choice gates the public flip
- `docs/install/{ubuntu,arch,nix,macos,wsl}.md`, `docs/release-runbook.md`, README install section, 7 `docs/research/release-*.md` reports; CLAUDE.md stale test-map row fixed

## Blast Radius

- **Additive for all existing flows**: no DB migrations, no schema-version bumps, no API/wire changes; `tests.yml`/`e2e.yml` changes are new jobs + stub consolidation only.
- **Behavior change, release (`!cgo`) builds only**: `--redaction maximum` (and config `redaction: maximum` at push/redact/harvest) now hard-errors instead of being unavailable-by-build-failure; cgo builds (dev shell, `make build`) are byte-identical in behavior. This was the user-selected Plan-UAT amendment ("never silently weaker redaction").
- **Nothing publishes externally**: `aurs`/`homebrew_casks` are `skip_upload: true`; repo is private; tags namespace `v*` cannot collide with `pkg/schema/v*`.
